title: 10 Best Career Options in Psychology
content:
Your Roadmap to a Career in Psychology in India 

 

Hushed conversations about mental health are history; today, we boldly address our concerns out in the open! India is breaking the silence for good. As we face work stress and daily challenges head-on, the need for mental health experts is on the rise. This growth also means more chances for exciting careers in this field.

In psychology, success isn't limited to one area. You can build a successful career brick by brick in various fields like clinical, forensic, educational, and more. 

Choosing psychology as a career has become popular because it can positively impact people's lives. However, it's crucial to recognize that there is a noticeable difference in the salaries of various psychology professions in India.

 

 

 

Exciting Careers in Psychology 

 

In the global academic landscape, psychology emerges as a top choice for undergraduate students, capturing their fascination and dedication as they view it not just as a field of study but as a promising full-time career.

The beauty of this field lies in its flexibility; you can seamlessly integrate it into your academic journey, considering it not only as a primary career path but also as a dynamic second option. Imagine pairing majors in other subjects with a minor in psychology, broadening your skill set and enhancing your marketability in today’s professional world. 

Intriguingly, the mental health sector itself has experienced a significant boost, with a reported 30% rise in the use of psychological services in the past few years.

 

Here in India, the field of psychology is undergoing a fascinating transformation, offering an exciting spectrum of career paths to explore. Whether clinical psychology, educational psychology, organizational psychology, or any other specialized branch, the possibilities are endless. The growing awareness surrounding mental health and well-being has changed the demand for skilled professionals, resulting in many career prospects in psychology. As individuals increasingly acknowledge the important role of mental health in their lives, the demand for trained experts to guide them has never been more pronounced. Opting for career opportunities in psychology not only empowers you to create a positive impact on people's lives but also presents the thrilling opportunity to navigate a dynamic and fulfilling professional journey. It's not just a career; it's a chance to be part of a transformative and deeply meaningful adventure.

 

 

 

In this blog, you will explore the most thrilling career paths in the field of psychology

 

Clinical Psychologist: Clinical psychologists are experts in mental health who assist people in dealing with feelings, behaviors, and mental health difficulties. They check and identify problems, offer therapy, and create plans to make overall well-being better. If someone is going through tough times like feeling sad or worried, clinical psychologists are there to help and support them in living healthier and happier lives.

 

Child Psychologist: Child psychologists are experts who focus on understanding and helping with the special feelings and actions of kids. They work with young people to check how they're growing, handle behavior issues, and offer support for their feelings. Using methods that are right for their age, child psychologists help kids deal with problems and learn important skills for life.

 

Industrial-Organizational Psychologist: Industrial-organizational psychologists are experts who look at how things work in a workplace to make it better for both the workers and the company. They learn about what makes employees happy, how to make them more productive, and ways to keep them feeling good. These psychologists use what they know about how the mind works to help companies make nice workspaces, build strong teams, and come up with plans to help employees grow and do well in their jobs.

 

Educational Psychologist: Educational psychologists focus on figuring out how people learn and grow in school. They look at things like how our brains work and how feelings affect learning. These experts also help with special needs in education, creating plans to make learning better. They team up with teachers, parents, and students to make sure classrooms are great places for learning. 

 

Counseling Psychologist: Counseling psychologists are here to help people deal with different life problems like stress, relationship troubles, and personal growth. They use different helpful methods to promote good mental and emotional health. These psychologists work with all kinds of people, providing support, advice, and strategies to cope with the ups and downs of life. They are like friendly guides, helping individuals navigate through life's challenges. 

 

Sports Psychologist: Sports psychologists are experts who focus on the mind and emotions in sports and physical activities. They team up with athletes to improve mental strength, focus, and overall performance. These specialists tackle concerns like nervousness, staying motivated, and setting goals. By assisting athletes in fine-tuning their mental well-being, sports psychologists help them perform at their very best in their chosen sports.

title: 10 Things to remember while choosing a mental health app
content:
We have an app for almost everything today. Maybe you want to learn a new language or buy a last-minute gift for a friend, there is an application for every problem a person faces, and thankfully mental health has also been catching on with technology. Due to long waiting lists and the post-pandemic culture of having access to everything from the comfort of your home, using a mental health application might look like a viable option. Not only is it cost-effective, but it also lets you have access to help without having to move anywhere.

 

Mental health applications usually use tools like therapy chatbots, mood tracking devices, and games to help people with various issues ranging from anxiety, and addiction to serious cases of depression and mood disorders. However, it is important to remember that not all apps are regulated and while some me be considered useful and safe, others might lack research and accuracy. Thousands of apps pertain to mental health available for users worldwide. But how to make an informed decision about which one to download on your phone? Well, we have compiled a list of pertinent things to consider before signing up for a mental health app, and considering them while making a decision can help you find what you are looking for.

 

Your mental health app checklist: 10 Things to consider 

 

1. Credibility: 

It is rare to find apps that are perfectly backed up by research and studies. While some apps do provide evidence of clinical trials and studies performed to prove their effectiveness, most commercial apps do not have that. Therefore, to ensure you do not end up with an unreliable application, you can check out the app’s website first. Reliable apps document their research and findings on their website to support their users.

 

2. Privacy and security: 

This is probably the most important aspect to consider while looking for a mental health app. What are the details asked of you? Are they seeking your location? Does the privacy policy inform you of how your data will be handled? Make sure to pose these questions while checking out apps. At the very least, they must have a good privacy policy in place to secure your information. Some apps have a feature where your data is not saved, securing privacy but this may not work if you are seeking help more than once. Knowing what you are signing up for can be incredibly useful.

 

3. Disclosure to therapist: 

You must most definitely disclose your attempts with mental health applications to your counselor or therapist. This way they can guide and give feedback that can enhance your app experience. Who better to tell you what is great for you than your reliable therapist? In case you do not have a therapist of your own and it is your first time seeking help, still, make sure to mention your experience if and when you do make an appointment with a professional.

 

4. Cost and services: 

So, the great thing about mental health apps is their prices and offers. Most of the apps let you gain access to basic services without paying anything, so it is free! Only some might have paid options if you wish to avail of advanced services. Thus, you will be spending way less than a regular offline appointment.

 

5. Reasonable goals: 

The key to finding the right mental health app is to first know what you are looking for. For example, you are in search of a vegetable shop, but let’s say you are looking for a specific one like cherry tomatoes or purple cabbage. You won't find these in all local stores, so knowing what to buy leads you to a supermarket or a commercial outlet that sells such exotic vegetables. Similarly, are you looking to track your mood, have a feeling diary, or talk to someone? Think about what drives you to these apps and then consider possible options to choose from.

 

 

6. Benefits of mental health apps: 

The benefits are pretty straightforward. Mental health apps are cost-effective, easily accessible, most user-friendly, and cover a wide range of issues and concerns. Make sure to go through the services they offer and compare them to find the right one for you.

 

7. User Experience: 

Also referred to as UX, is your overall experience of using the application. Whether it was interesting to use or engaging enough that you kept coming back to it, user experience defines these aspects. But how do we know the UX even before using the application? Look for reviews by people who have already used the app and check out the screenshots of the app design and how it will look while you use it. These things will help you get a hang of the app and then you can select/reject depending on what you like.

 

8. It may not work for everyone: 

Yes, mental health apps are great, but they may not work for everyone. The responses vary just like they do with other methods of healing. While maintaining that apps are not completely unhelpful, it is important to know that if it didn’t work for someone, doesn’t mean it won’t work for you and vice-versa.

 

9. Apps do not replace professional therapy: 

In the end, you must understand that apps are just computerized bots trying to respond to what you type or speak. The personal touch of an actual person who can see you and help is beyond compare. Also, mental health professionals are trained people whereas, applications aren’t.

 

10. Apps can work alongside professional therapy: 

Apps are mainly used as a self-help measure, something to help you understand what is going on with you. Many professionals like to recommend apps to supplement therapy, this way you get the best of both worlds.

 

The Trail and error method of selecting an app

 

Many try a few apps and then decide which one really works for them. With so many free applications out there, the choices are endless. If you have the time in hand, go ahead and try some of the top mental health applications and see how they can help you. This method takes up a lot of time and effort for investigation but in the end, it can be rewarding if you find the right mental health application.

title: 10 tips how to become an Industrial Organizational Psychologist
content:
In today's dynamic workplace landscape, the entry of gen z marks the begining of a new era. Big companies are constantly looking for highly skilled professionals who can streamline operations and give a competitive edge to the organization. In sync with this thought, Industrial-Organizational Psychologists are rightly skilled to address these multifaceted challenges and drive companies towards success in the evolving job market.

 

Scope of Industrial-Organizational Psychology

The people of a company are the greatest asset behind its success.

 

In today's business landscape, companies have been actively hiring industrial-organizational psychologists who can understand employee behavior and play a pivotal role in building effective strategies that can optimize internal processes across key development areas. These areas include recruitment, training and development, employee performance and motivation, and organizational development and structure.

 

Industrial-organizational psychologists deeply engage with the business world, by focussing on improving organizational effectiveness. They play two important roles: facilitating creation of a sustainable environment in the workplace, ensuring the wellbeing and satisfaction of employees; and developing streamlined processes to boost the productivity and profitability for the organization.

 

 

 

Industrial Psychology Salary:  

PayScale states the annual salary for I/O psychologists in India to be approximately RS 62,00,000 with a range of RS 39,00,000 to RS 1,02,00,000. This industry has been witnessing significant growth, offering abundant career opportunities to individuals within prominent organizations.

 

As this field is growing in India, companies have begun to acknowledge the importance of organizational culture, employee-wellbeing, and performance enhancement in contributing to a successful business. As companies strive to maintain a competitive edge in the dynamic market landscape of today, the demand for skilled I/O psychologists has been on the rise.

 

Furthermore, the career prospects are flourishing correspondingly, spanning diverse sectors like information technology, manufacturing, healthcare, and finance. In simple words, I/O psychologists have become the true catalysts sparking innovation in the workplace and bringing in positive transformations.  

 

Look at these 10 tips on how to become an Industrial-Organizational Psychologist

Industrial-Organizational (I-O) Psychology is a dynamic field that combines principles of psychology with organizational behavior to improve workplace environments and productivity.

 

1. LISTENING

Listening skills play a very important role in this field, enabling you to understand the multifaceted needs of individuals and their organizations. While some already have it in them, others develop the skill with time and training.  

 

2. PROBLEM SOLVING

Problem solving is the ability of an I/O psychologist to aptly work through challenges as and when they arise, within organizational structures or interpersonal relationships. As a problem solver, you also become a neutral mediator, who excels at identifying the core issues affecting the workplace, and someone who develops equitable solutions in alignment with the company’s goals and objectives.  

 

3. NEGOTIATION & PERSUASION

Be it resolving disputes, finalizing compensation packages, or settling arguments, you will always find yourself at the forefront of negotiations, while working as an I/O psychologist. Your skill in this regard lies in finding mutually beneficial outcomes and articulating persuasive arguments, which are instrumental in fostering productive collaborations and resolving conflicts.  

 

4. DATA ANALYSIS

As an I/O psychologist, your proficiency in quantitative analysis is the most important, especially in people analytics. You must be able to leverage data to inform strategic decisions, right from recruitment processes to organizational assessments. Having strong analytical skills boosts your efficiency and enhances your marketability as well as income potential in the field.  

 

5. WRITING & READING COMPREHENSION

Proficiency in both writing and comprehending complex materials is essential, considering the significance of written documentation in this industry. Writing and reading comprehension ensures clarity and transparency in organizational operations, from drafting policies, interpreting legal documents, or analyzing agreements.  

 

6. BUSINESS ACUMEN

A thorough understanding of the organization's business model, objectives, and challenges is imperative for driving impactful interventions. Companies seek professionals versed in industrial-organizational psychology who can proactively contribute to operational enhancements and strategic initiatives, making business acumen an asset in your arsenal.  

 

7. SOCIAL SKILLS

Given the inherently people-centric nature of industrial-organizational psychology roles, honing your social skills is paramount. The ability to engage in meaningful conversations, interpret social cues, and empathize with others sets the stage for fostering positive relationships and driving organizational success. Prioritizing the development of emotional intelligence further amplifies your effectiveness in navigating interpersonal dynamics within the workplace. 

 

8. TEACHING & LEARNING

Roles in industrial-organizational psychology typically mandate ongoing employee training and continuous professional development. If you possess a passion for both imparting and acquiring knowledge, you're primed for success in this domain. By embracing the opportunities for learning and growth inherent in the field, you position yourself for achievement and fulfillment in your career journey. 

 

9. MANAGEMENT

In industrial-organizational psychology, leadership and management skills stand as cornerstones for success. The ability to strategize, coordinate, recruit, and develop talent is indispensable. Therefore, the golden rule is constant improvement of your management skills. By prioritizing the improvement of these skills, you pave the path for effective organizational leadership and sustained professional growth. 

 

10. COMMUNICATION

For an industrial-organizational psychologist, the ability to articulate thoughts clearly is most important. Effective communication includes not only the words you choose but also the tone and body language you convey, as these factors heavily influence how your messages are interpreted and received. Mastering communication skills in all its facets is important for fostering understanding, interaction, and positive outcomes in organizational settings.

title: A beginner in psychology? Here’s how you can get the basics right
content:
“Get the fundamentals down and the level of everything you do will rise”

– Michael Jordan

 

 

Apart from being one of the most popular subjects being chosen as a major across the world, psychology is also a great source of understanding how the human mind and behaviour work.

As someone who has just started their journey towards understanding and studying psychology, it is important to get the basics right. Whether it is about comprehending the scope of the subject or putting together major sources of information from the right place, it is crucial that you know what you’re dealing with. Today there are a million ways to learn more about the human mind and behaviour just by the click of a button. The Internet today has become a sourcing hub of tools, resources, and information on the wide world of psychology. 

 

You can either sign up for a beginner’s online course, put in a few extra hours on your college course, or practice self-studying using online resources. When it comes to learning there are endless ways to do so. However, the study of the human mind mainly works around a few predominant topics that are central to the subject. Let us look get the various fundamentals of psychology and the right way to get the basics right.

 

Stepping into the world of psychology 

 

As a beginner in the field, you must always start with the basics. Learning about psychology is not just about knowing how to help people, you must also be well-acquainted with what psychology is and the rich history of the subject. Learning about the early history and findings in psychology is a major topic for every aspirant and shall also be a part of your curriculum. Another major topic covered in psychology is the various branches of psychology that form the very foundation of understanding what the subject is all about and what it is not. While the history part will always keep coming up in this field, knowing the origin, major contributors, and milestones in the history of psychology is a good place to start.

 

Developmental psychology

 

Being one of the largest sub-fields in psychology, developmental psychology covers aspects of development and change during each stage of your lifespan. The importance of this field came to light when it was realised that childhood has a significant role to play and is a unique part of life that defines the course of our future behaviours and traits. It may seem like the subject is very easy as it is something you have gone through. However, with time you will realise that there are many complexities to the topic and much more to learn than you imagined. The subject also includes various questions and concerns of psychologists, their opinions, and the knowledge hub accumulated by them. It is worth your time to dig deep into all of these topics to learn about developmental psychology, forming a strong foundation for your psychology career.

 

Research Methodology

 

The question that makes your brain ich is, “How do psychologists or researchers study the human brain?”. Well, it is important to have a basic comprehension of research methods used to investigate the human mind and why people behave the way they do. You may not want to get into the field of research in psychology, nevertheless, in any sub-field you choose, you will be dealing with research conducted by psychologists. Learning the various approaches to studying human behaviours is integral to this field and can give you a better view of things while studying.

 

Behavioural Psychology

 

One of the most influential branches of psychology is behavioural psychology or behaviourism which emerged during the 20th century and is relevant till today. Behaviour forms the central part of any person and is a crucial indicator of psychological distress. The principles of behavioural psychology are heavily used in all kinds of training, therapy, and education. However, behaviourism is not as popular as it was once, although knowing the basic principles will help you understand the subject better. Concepts like classical conditioning and operant conditioning are pertinent to every psychology student and also form a great part of psychology literature. This branch focuses on identifying and changing behaviour patterns and knowing about reinforcements and punishments will help you master the subject.

 

Social Psychology

 

Have you ever noticed that sometimes in a social setting people tend to act differently? Also, when we are around people, our thoughts and behaviour is greatly influenced by their presence. Social psychology is a branch that essentially seeks to understand the social behaviour of a person including their interaction with others and how that influences behaviour. A lot of concepts can be covered in social psychology and it is also considered one of the most fascinating fields of psychology.

 

Personality and its dysfunctions

 

As a beginner in psychology, another major topic of interest is personality. You may know that personalities are something unique to everyone and a major part of who we are. There are many theories formulated by psychologists that are centred on understanding how a personality is formed or developed. Major questions in this field include; What factors influence our personalities? Is personality change possible or is it a fixed set of traits? What a personality disorders and how to get over them? This and much more, when you start learning you'll realise personality has a whole lot of literature and theories.

 

Theories and schools of thought

 

From Freud, and Erikson to Jung, many prominent thinkers came up with theories and thoughts that have necessarily shaped the subject of psychology. Although you will be learning about some of the most common ones like the Freudian theory of psychosexual development, The Big 5 theory of personality, and Maslow’s hierarchy of needs, just to name a few. These concepts and theories, although no longer in use will still be an important part of your study. Being thorough with the basic theories will help you gain useful insight on the subject.

 

Interestingly, these topics are the very basics of the dynamic study of the human mind, essentially the tip of the iceberg, and have a long way to go. Having said that, it is also what will make you a great psychology student and potentially a great psychologist one day.

title: A Necessary Skill: Basics of APA Format you should know
content:
Are you a psychology student looking to write your first research paper or any other psychological writing? If that is the case, then you will have to familiarise yourself with the APA format to successfully organise and reference your paper appropriately. If you have not heard about the APA format before, it might seem a little confusing from the writing and formatting style you must have been accustomed to.

 

A consistent format was necessary for readers from across the world to recognize research work and understand the nitty-gritty of it. While it may seem like a daunting task, learning APA style writing is a highly useful skill that will prove beneficial to you for a long time. Let us first understand what APA Format is and why is it the pinnacle of research writing.

 

The Meaning of APA Format

 

APA format is the official style of the American Psychological Association, abbreviated as APA, a common format used to cite sources in not just psychology but also other disciplines like economics, social sciences, nursing, business, etc. The origin of this standard style can be traced back to 1929 when an article published in the Psychological Bulletin laid down the basic guidelines. Later, the expansion of the same was documented in the Publication Manual of the American Psychological Association and is being referred to by students and professionals all around.

 

You might wonder why is APA format so important for psychology students to be thorough with? Well, the APA style is a standard way of writing research pieces in a way that researchers and students are able to effectively communicate their ideas to the world in a consistent manner. This allows the readers to know what they are looking for and sets them apart from other forms of writing.

 

The format lays down a consistent way to acknowledge the work of others by providing a comprehensive set of guidelines as to structure, format, writing, and grammar that can rightfully cite sources.

 

In case you have never written any paper before, it might seem intimidating also considering that many universities and colleges have their own set of guidelines (although all of them are loosely inspired by the APA format itself). Many times, universities use formats distinct from the APA style so much that the students find it difficult to tune themselves in the APA style. Might as well go through a difficult transition now than ever as APA is a global style and will help you grasp pieces of literature in a better manner. It is an essential skill for every psychology or social science student.

 

Basics of APA Format: Key sections of your paper 

 

Typically, every paper will have these four key sections, namely, the title page, abstract, main body, and references list. Let us look at each of them in the light of the APA format:

 

1. Title Page: The purpose of the title page is to let the readers know at a glance about who you are and what you are here with. Make sure you include the title, the author’s name, and college affiliation. Apart from that, the page must also show details of your course study (name and number), your instructor’s name, and the date on which the paper is due. Like every other paper you might have written or read before this, the title must be catchy and must justify the essence of your topic without being too mainstream or mundane.

 

2. The Abstract: Immediately following the title page is the abstract. An abstract is nothing but a summary of what your paper is going to be about. In APA style, you should keep your abstract restricted to up to 200 words, 100 words bring the minimum criteria. Although these numbers will vary depending on instructor requirements and publication rules.

The abstract must essentially have these components:

 

a) The goal of your paper.

b) State hypothesis if any.

c) Methods and participants used (briefly).

d) Main findings that will be dealt with by your paper.

e) Conclusions and significance of your findings.

 

3. Main Body: The exact format of the body may vary as per the kind of paper you are writing. For example, if you are writing a lab report then sections like introduction, results, and discussion will be inserted. The main body is the central piece of your paper and will contain the entire essay itself. It will be helpful to check the guidelines provided by your university for more clarification on this subject. The specifics may differ, but the main body must include all that surrounds your topic, including a good conclusion.

 

4. References: Now comes the most important aspect of your paper, references. References refer to giving detailed information on all the various sources you gathered the information from for your paper. It is advisable to always begin this section from a new page.

 

If there is any piece of information that you have cited (reproduce findings by others as evidence for your argument) in your paper, it must be in the reference section. Also, obviously, every reference cited in the reference section must be mentioned somewhere in your paper. A few pointers to remember while writing this section:

 

> List your references alphabetically by the last name of the authors.

> Materials/books by the same author must be listed in chronological order from oldest to most recent.

> Do not change the nature of the text from sources, be it punctuation or capitalization, keep it as is.

> All book titles, journals, magazines, and newspapers, the titles should be italicized.

> As to formatting, all references should be doubled spaced, the first line each line flush left, with additional lines to be indented.

 

4. In-text Citations: It is vital to include citations in your paper identifying the source of the information you have used. These are called in-text citations and the APA format insists that while citing within the text of your paper the author's name should be followed by the date of publication. However, the extended information about the source should be included in the reference section in detail.

 

Tips for Beginners in APA Format

 

For those who find APA paper writing confusing it will be better to start with these manageable steps:

 

1. When you begin doing your research create an outline and a working bibliography that will help you keep track of all the references you use right from the beginning.

 

2. Abstract should always be written in the last so that it accurately summarises your paper. You may be tempted to start with the abstract but delaying it till the end will do justice to your paper. 

 

3. As a rule use past tense or past perfect or present perfect tense throughout your research paper (e.g.: “was”, “has been” “have been”, etc). Try not to use contractions in your paper such as “it hasn’t”, instead use “it has not”.

 

4. For references make sure that you keep track of all your sources. Also using citation tools can be a great way to manage and organise your references accurately.

 

5. Review your finished paper to ensure that all the citations and formatting are up to the mark.

 

A word from the wise

 

The APA format may not be universally followed exactly, however, every format that your school or university uses is loosely based on the APA format which is the standard format when it comes to psychological research writing. Over the years there have been many changes and editions to the official publication manual of the APA format. Many online sites offer helpful tips and let you access the latest version of the publication for you to follow. Maybe writing a research paper seems like a lot of work right now but understanding the basic rules of APS style can be a huge help and can come in handy in the future.

title: Abnormal Psychology
content:
Abnormal Psychology: Know more than what you’ve heard

 

The use of the term ‘abnormal’ has been the subject of considerable debate in the recent past. What exactly is ‘normal’ and who distinguishes normality and abnormality is another spectrum of this debate. The social norms dictate and determine what is normal versus abnormal behaviour and this definition will keep changing over time. Therefore, the concept of abnormality is imprecise, and very hard to confine it into a standard definition.

 

Abnormal psychology has been an important branch of psychology since its inception dealing with psychopathology and abnormal behaviour comes more often in a clinical setup. It is the division of psychology that investigates and studies people who are atypical or abnormal in comparison to the other members of a given society. Clinical psychologists, psychotherapists, and counselors mainly work in this field of psychology. As an aspirant of psychology or a professional, understanding the history of abnormal psychology and its present status is crucial. This blog will discuss the basics of abnormal psychology and how it is different from other areas of psychology. Also, we will dwell on the definition of abnormality and the known criticisms of this branch.

 

Abnormal Psychology: Meaning and definition

 

Abnormal psychology primarily focuses on signs of mental health conditions through your emotions, thoughts, and behaviour. As opposed to bifurcating behaviour into normal and abnormal, psychologists in this field try to assess the level of distress that your thoughts, emotions, and behaviours might cause. Any behaviour of an individual that derails him or her from leading a life without problems would constitute abnormal behaviour. Where a person’s life is being affected or there are disruptive results to a particular behaviour, those, in the opinion of psychologists in this field, require some sort of mental health intervention and treatment. Abnormal psychology as a branch is streamlined towards understanding and studying psychopathology and disruptive behaviour in a clinical context.

 

The concept of abnormality is very difficult to define. Where at first sight a definition may seem reasonable, a closer look will reveal how problematic it can be. Due to this ambiguity, it is important to understand the several different ways in which a possible definition for ‘abnormal’ can be given against our idea of what is ‘normal’ and what is not.

 

Definitions of Abnormality

 

1. Statistical Infrequency: Under this definition, a person’s trait, behaviour, and thinking are classified as abnormal if it is rare or unusual. However, this does not serve as a sufficient definition because even some healthy and beneficial behaviours occur infrequently. Just because something is unusual or uncommon it does not mean that it is abnormal.

 

2. Distress-inducing: Abnormal behaviours are seen as those that disturb the peace of an individual or be disruptive to others.

 

3. Socially Disruptive: Based on the sociological definition, such behaviour is considered violative of social norms. People with abnormal behaviour would find it difficult to operate in social settings and maintain long-lasting or even brief, social relationships.

 

4. Affects the ability to function: Where usual functionality in daily life is being affected along with a disturbance in relationships, work, and personal life, it is indicative of abnormal behaviour. Such people come under the radar of abnormal psychology as the ability to function normally, even in a secure place, is highly lacking.

 

Scope of Abnormal Psychology

 

Largely, abnormal psychology studies psychological disorders, their diagnosis, treatment, and prevention. Psychological disorders are patterns of behaviour or clinical symptoms that impact multiple areas of a person’s life. These conditions put the person experiencing the symptoms in deep distress. Mental health professionals in the field use the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM) published by the American Psychiatric Association (APA). The DSM is a reference manual for professionals containing a list of psychiatric disorders, diagnostic codes, and relevant information for each disorder and diagnostic criteria. Additionally, the International Classification of Diseases (ICD) is another globally used diagnostic tool for epidemiology and clinical purposes maintained by the World Health Organization (WHO).

 

These manuals have characterised psychological disorders into multiple sections some of which include, mood disorders, anxiety disorders, neurodevelopmental disorders, personality disorders, substance use disorders, and neurocognitive disorders, such as delirium, etc.

 

Approaches of Abnormal Psychology

 

1. Behavioural: This area of study looks for observable behaviours that can be reinforced with positive behaviour through therapy. This approach to abnormal psychology only targets behaviour and not its underlying causes.

 

2. Medical: This approach of abnormal psychology looks for biological causes of mental illness and its underlying cause including genetic inheritance physical illness and chemical imbalances. Treatment is focused on medicines along with some type of psychotherapy.

 

3. Cognitive: The cognitive approach attempts to understand how perceptions, thoughts, and reasoning that happens internally, can be a cause for psychological disorders. Therefore, even cognitive treatments are focused on helping individuals change their thoughts or reactions.

 

4. Psychoanalytic: This Freud-influenced approach suggests abnormal behaviours grow from unconscious desires, thoughts, and memories. It believes that the feelings that are outside of our awareness influence our conscious actions.

 

Criticisms of Abnormal Psychology

 

There is no doubt that the field of abnormal psychology is under major scrutiny. The usage of the word ‘abnormal’ itself is highly problematic. In addition to debates over the use of the term itself, there are also other shortcomings observed by many.

 

In a way, the field stigmatizes vulnerable and oppressed people and tends to monger pathology on normal variations of human behaviour. Critics also suggest that the medical approach to mental illness is restricted to biological and genetic factors of distress rather than taking a broader view of the distress-causing behaviour. It also does not account for the fact that what is normal and abnormal is based on cultural differences, leading to a rudimental approach to mental illness. Certain studies also found that learning about abnormal psychology was not that effective in reducing mental health stigma and improving attitudes toward it. It is pertinent to understand that abnormal psychology is not trying to fit people into a narrow definition of normal but focuses on identifying and treating problematic behaviour.

title: Addressing Mental Health Stigma: How Indian Cinema is Contributing to Change
content:
Bollywood Cinema & Mental Illness 

The evolution of mental health portrayals in Indian cinema has now led to a more thoughtful and compassionate approach. Rather than giving way to sensationalism and mockery, Bollywood has begun to depict characters struggling with mental health issues in a much more balanced and realistic manner. The change can be seen in how these characters are no longer one-dimensional stereotypes but very relatable, three-dimensional individuals who battle complex emotional challenges.  

 

Modern films explore the emotional turmoil, vulnerability, and strength and resilience of individuals dealing with mental health problems. Characters are now portrayed with much more depth and authenticity, thereby shifting the focus from superficial portrayals to realistic depictions. Clearly, Bollywood is now bringing to light the authentic struggles in managing mental health.  

Indian cinema boasts of a vast and diverse landscape, within which the concept of mental health has grown as a compelling and thought-provoking theme. It goes beyond the depths of human psychology, exploring the complexities of emotional wellbeing, and often serves as a mirror reflecting the diverse social stigmas surrounding mental health problems. In all these years, Indian cinema has begun a remarkable journey, witnessing the evolving of the portrayal of mental health, influencing public understanding, and redefining traditional narratives to promote understanding and awareness.  

 

Rewind to a couple of years ago, we are reminded of the days when Bollywood films would categorize almost every mental disorder as “ye paagal hain, inko paagalkhaane le jaaya jaaye” on black and white cinema. Coming back to present times, we hear of films like 2007’s “Bhool Bhulaiya” which dealt with dissociative identity disorder, and 2016’s “Dear Zindagi”, where the protagonist battles depression. Most of these movies left a lasting impression to the audience, including “Hichki” and “Chicchore”, which dealt with turette syndrome, exam anxiety and suicide.

 

 

What is commendable is how  to arrive at a clearer picture of these illnesses that they choose to depict on the screen.  

 

Another major factor that has immensely contributed to the way in which mental health has been perceived by the public is the awareness that their favorite actors have gone through the same. Eminent personalities like Deepika Padukone and Anushka Sharma have come out in the open to talk about their emotional struggles in recent times. As Padukone openly admitted her struggles with depression and became the brand ambassador of the Indian Psychiatric Society, these actors have become the role models that people have begun to look up to.  

 

Bollywood Films on Mental Health 

 

Directed by Gauri Shinde, “Dear Zindagi” is a true testament to the evolving landscape of Indian cinema. The film documents the complicated journey of the protagonist, Alia Bhatt, who navigates through the labyrinth of her emotional and mental landscape. The movie places a very strong emphasis on the importance of seeking professional help when you need it the most and embracing oneself. Truly, the film dismantles the age-old stigmas that revolve around mental health.  

“Taare Zameen Par” directed by Mr. Perfectionist, Amir Khan, depicts a child’s challenging battle with dyslexia. The film goes beyond surface-level portrayals, highlighting the profound impact of learning disorders on a child’s mental health. The movie serves as a poignant reminder of the critical and urgent need to understand and address the emotional burdens and struggles of youngsters.  

Director Vijay Lalwani, in his film “Karthik Calling Karthik” highlights in detail the complex world of dissociative identity disorder. The film’s protagonist, Farhan Akhtar, undergoes a transformative journey triggered by something as minor as a mysterious phone call! The cinematic narrative calls for a profound exploration of the complex interplay between identity, trauma, and mental health.  

 

 

 

Indian Cinema has unfolded significantly in recent years, but not restricting itself solely to being a source of entertainment but by trying to experiment in showcasing social and responsible cinema with an intent of having a stronger impact on the masses.  

To conclude, the portrayal of mental health in Bollywood has undergone a significant transformation, gradually evolving from traditional stereotypes and sensationalism to nuanced, empathetic narratives. Bollywood's journey from depicting mental illness through exaggerated, often stigmatizing lenses to presenting deeply human stories reflects a significant cultural shift. This commendable evolution reflects a broader societal transformation, where mental health is no longer relegated to the shadows but is brought into the light with sensitivity and accuracy. 

Modern films explore the emotional turmoil, vulnerability, and strength and resilience of individuals dealing with mental health problems. Characters are now portrayed with much more depth and authenticity, thereby shifting the focus from superficial portrayals to realistic depictions. Clearly, Bollywood is now bringing to light the authentic struggles in managing mental health. 

 

Indian cinema boasts of a vast and diverse landscape, within which the concept of mental health has grown as a compelling and thought-provoking theme. It goes beyond the depths of human psychology, exploring the complexities of emotional wellbeing, and often serves as a mirror reflecting the diverse social stigmas surrounding mental health problems. In all these years, Indian cinema has begun a remarkable journey, witnessing the evolving of the portrayal of mental health, influencing public understanding, and redefining traditional narratives to promote understanding and awareness. 

As Indian filmmakers increasingly collaborate with mental health professionals to ensure authentic representation, these films are not just becoming cinematic experiences but powerful catalysts for change. They challenge outdated norms, foster empathy, and encourage open conversations about mental health, paving the way for greater awareness and understanding. 

The involvement of celebrities who openly share their personal battles with mental health issues further amplifies this message. Their bravery in confronting their struggles publicly not only humanizes these issues but also inspires countless individuals to reach out for help and support. 

Indian cinema’s role in addressing mental health stigma is a true testament to the power of storytelling in shaping societal attitudes. It continues to push boundaries and offer authentic portrayals; Bollywood is contributing to a cultural narrative that prioritizes mental well-being and fosters a more compassionate society. Moving forward, it is essential to support and celebrate this positive shift, recognizing the significant role cinema plays in transforming perceptions and encouraging a more inclusive dialogue about mental health.

title: Become a successful Counsellor in India: #Top 3 Insider tips!
content:
Statistically speaking, India has a youth population of 400 million. Out of this total, only 5000 are professionally trained Counsellors. This is a significant gap in the industry that needs to be bridged. Considering the spurt in student population every year, the country is growing as a hotspot for aspiring career Counsellors. Clearly, it is amongst the most rewarding careers of all times. With the right set of efforts, knowledge, and persuasiveness, you too could become a successful career Counsellor and earn up to 6 lakhs INR, with an average annual salary of 2.7 lakhs. 

The key challenge to becoming a professional and certified career Counsellor is to align your career interest with perfectly used psychometric tests. 

Know about the top 3 steps to become a successful career Counsellor in India, and make use of proven tactics to become the masters of the field. 

So if you are looking for effective ways to kickstart your Counselling career, this guide is your ideal fit! 

Who is a Counsellor? 

A Counsellor is an expert who helps people with problems by providing professional advice on personal matters, emotional difficulties, career complications, and relationship problems. The boon of a successful Counsellor is the remarkable ability to empathize with a deeper understanding of human emotions.Counselling or talking therapy encompasses several aspects related to mental health and emotional wellbeing 

How can you become a Counsellor? 

Anyone can become a Counsellor as long as they share a passion for helping people and motivating them to find constructive solutions that would bring positive change in their lives. Any Counsellor has the following set of responsibilities: 

1. Ability to understand the perspectives and problems of their client.

2. Helping clients define their goals and plan of action.

3. Developing pathways to achieve those goals.

4. Act as a facilitator to help accomplish those goals.

5. Focus on the holistic development of the individual.

Top skills required to ace your Counselling game:

1. Building a comfortable relationship with your client

When a prospective client reaches out to you for the purpose of personal Counselling, you must ensure that you build a warm relationship with him/her, so as to offer them a safe space. This ensures the building of mutual trust and confidence, so as to ensure that your client avoids hesitation while discussing his/her problems. 

2. Careful analysis through personality tests

The assessment forms the most important part of any Counselling session. It is in this stage that the Counsellor absorbs all details regarding the problems, conducts personality tests, and comprehends their root cause. Every minute detail is taken into consideration, including the specific reactions to each question asked. It is after careful assessment and evaluation of all problems that the goal of the entire session is decided and settled. 

3. Selection of goals

It is after careful evaluation of all the problems and issues, that the Counsellor finally decides to fix the goal of the session. This goal could be aimed either towards overcoming the hindrance or working on reconciliation. 

4. Plan of action

The plan of action is formulated to see effective results. An example could be in terms of a client who has a fear of speaking in public. In such a case, the Counsellor may ask him/her to practice speaking in front of a mirror. The client’s improvement is assessed throughout the duration of the plan of action and when they reach normalcy, the final stage is said to be reached. However, in certain cases, the plan of action may be changed depending on whether the client shows improvement or not. 

5. Overcoming the main problem

As has been already mentioned, if the execution of the set plan of action reaps benefits for the client in terms of marked improvement in his/her behavioral patterns, then the goal of overcoming the problem is finally accomplished. This is when the Counsellor becomes successful in their task. 

Resources available for upskilling: 

There are several resources available for aspiring Counsellors which will help them level up their skills and aid in better knowledge enhancement and skill refinement. In a general sense, there are several platforms that guide you to become a professional. 

Given below is a brief list of all the useful resources that you may and should take advantage of, if you want to become an expert in the field: 

1. Participate in formal courses and workshops

2. Attend industry webinars and conferences

3. Reach out to the right mentors who can provide right guidance

4. Follow all industry-trends by reading blogs, articles, and publications

5. Set yourself manageable milestones

Top career options as a Counsellor in India: 

 

1. Career Counsellor

2. Corporate Counsellor

3. Credit Counsellor

4. Genetic Counsellor

5. Loan Counsellor

6. Mental Health Counsellor

7. Prison Counsellor

8. Rehabilitation Counsellor

title: Best Psychology Courses
content:
Studying psychology opens doors to understanding people's thoughts, emotions, and behaviors, making it an exciting and impactful field. It's not just about helping others; it's also about understanding ourselves better. Considering courses in psychology offers a chance to delve into diverse areas, from counselling to forensic psychology, allowing you to explore your interests and find your niche. To find the best courses, you must look for accredited programs with experienced faculty, practical learning opportunities, and a curriculum that aligns with your career goals. The best courses often offer a balance between theoretical knowledge and hands-on experience, preparing you for a fulfilling career in this captivating field.

 

Get ready to explore the best psychology courses that'll fuel your passion for understanding people's minds and behaviors. Whether you're fascinated by the theories of the brain or eager to help others through counselling, these courses are your gateway to a fascinating journey. This blog post will bring to you the best psychology courses that will spark your interest and set the way for an exciting learning adventure! 

 

As previously discussed, when choosing the best course, keep in mind factors like accreditation, course curriculum, faculty expertise, and reviews from past students to find one that aligns with your learning goals and interests in psychology.

 

Here are some of the best psychology courses in India: 

 

1. Clinical Psychology:

Clinical psychology is all about understanding and helping people with mental health issues, irrational behavior, or problems with their mind. It's about giving complete care and help for these difficult mental health problems. Besides working with individuals, clinical psychologists also look at helping couples, families, and groups.

 

2. Counselling Psychology:

Counselling Psychology is a kind of health service that helps people feel better and cope with problems by using lots of different ways that respect different cultures. It's about preventing troubles, helping when things get tough, and making life better for people. This kind of psychology mainly focuses on how people grow up and get better in life, trying to prevent problems and teaching things that help. It also knows a lot about work and career problems.

 

3. Industrial-Organizational Psychology:

Industrial-organizational (I-O) psychology helps with work problems using psychology ideas and ways. These I-O psychologists often team up with human resources, research, and marketing groups in companies. They mainly look at things like handling problems between workers, fixing conflicts, and hiring, training, and checking workers. Lots of I-O psychologists work in areas like teaching, advice, or government jobs. Getting a degree in industrial-organizational psychology can lead to good-paying jobs in many different fields.

 

4. Educational Psychology:

Educational psychology is about how people learn and remember things, especially in places like schools. It looks at feelings, getting along with others, and thinking when it comes to learning. They might study how to teach better, different ways to test students, and how to make classrooms better for learning. People who study this might become teachers, education experts, or work in jobs like studying how well programs work, testing, or doing research in schools, government, or businesses.

 

5. Social Psychology: 

Social psychology is a big part of psychology that looks at how we see ourselves and how people act in groups. Thus, it's about how people act because of others and the situations that make us feel and behave in social ways. Social psychology looks at lots of things like how we see ourselves, how we think in social situations, why we blame or think about things, how others affect us, how groups work, and how we treat each other.

title: Breaking the Silence on Financial Stress on Men
content:
For a long time, society has expected men to be the sole earners in the family. This has conditioned men to deal with financial pressure without complaining. 

“The breadwinners,” “The financial pillars of their families” – this image of men has been ingrained in our culture for generations. While gender roles are evolving, the pressure on men to be the provider of the family still remains strong. No doubt, this unsaid expectation has a significant impact on men's mental health. 

 

Beyond the Stereotypes 

 

Bollywood and pop culture have displayed our HERO as the ideal “financially secure” person in the relationship. If not already financially secure, the hero must become financially secure to win over his lover’s father. We often see a happy ending with the hero gaining all the wealth and riches through his journey. 

But this journey from rags to riches is rare and far from glamorous. Men experiencing financial strain often suffer in silence, suppress their emotions leading to unhealthy coping mechanisms like eating disorders, alcohol, bad company and more. 

Mental health problems are increasing in India. A study from Pew Research Center indicates that men are twice as likely to feel the financial burden in a relationship compared to women. Another report states: The Accidental Deaths & Suicides in India 2021 reports a 72.5-to-27.5 male-to-female ratio of suicide victims. Over 73,900 more men committed suicide in 2021 than women. 

 

Let's Talk About It 

 

There is a lot of scope to work in men’s mental health scape. As we enter June, known as Men’s Health Month, let’s explore how financial pressure has been affecting men and how we can take proactive steps towards men’s well-being. 

 

 

 

How to cope with financial stress? 

  1. Unlearning the Beliefs: 

We need to remind men that if women are breaking norms and reaching the moon, men need to get comfortable with the idea of not solely bearing financial burdens. Society needs to make them feel that it is fine and equally “manly” to take up roles like homemakers or share the earning responsibility. 

 

  1. It Is Okay Not to Be Okay: 

Seeking help from family, friends, or even organizations that offer financial aid or assistance is normal when you need it. 

 

  1. Practice Mindfulness Activities: 

Being mindful and resilient is important so you do not fall into peer pressure to spend extra money. Practice healthy habits such as eating well, exercising regularly, sleeping enough, meditating, or relaxing to cope with ongoing stress. 

 

  1. Seeking Professional Help: 

If you are going through any kind of financial stress, the first step should be to work on your mental health problems in India. If you are failing at the self-practice of being mindful, seek advice or assistance from financial experts or counselors. Counselors can address your problems both at the mental well-being level and guide you toward the right career path. 

 

  1. Upskilling: 

Invest in education or skills development to enhance your professional growth and career prospects. If you are someone passionate about making a change in the mental health sector, there is immense scope of work. Career counselling is something we all are looking for. You can train yourself with the available counselling programs to equip yourself to counsel and help others.  

 

 

 

 

What Can We Do to Change the Narrative for Men? 

 

  1. Raising Emotionally Intelligent Boys: 

For all young parents, teachers, and mentors, it is important to inculcate the right values in our children, especially boys, so they know how to deal with this pressure when it comes. Also, when the time comes, they are not the ones bullying fellow men for financial issues. 

 

  1. Creating a Resourceful Environment for Them: 

With social media, the day and age have come when there is already so much awareness and defense against stereotypes like these. Resources like financial advisory, skill development programs, counselor, and psychologist support are also on the rise. This will help men gather enough resources to cope with stress, anxiety, and mental health problems. 

 

  1. Educating Our Women: 

Women are increasingly playing a stronger role in the workforce, challenging traditional gender roles that have been around for a long time. By encouraging them further and creating opportunities for them as per their ambitions, we will make it easier for both genders to share the financial burdens. 

 

Before You Leave This Blog, 

 

Remember, the focus on mental health is a must. Mental well-being is as important as physical well-being. Men are dealing with the pressures of financial stability, family responsibility, peer pressure and many more evils of the society we ourselves have created. This Men’s Mental Health Awareness Month (June 2024) is a chance to encourage open conversations about challenges and share valuable resources that can support them. Let's together build a healthier future for all!

title: Build Your Very Own Mental Health First-Aid Kit
content:
Life has a very unusual way of throwing curveballs at you; when you least expect it. It could be relentless work pressure or even unexpected disappointments. Each one of us has had days that left us feeling either drained or falling out of sync. The larger question is, how do we keep it together when life decides to take us on an emotional rollercoaster ride?  

This is where the Mental Health First Aid Kit comes to your rescue! It is your personal collection of tools and strategies specifically designed to help you deal with the ups and downs of life with grace. Unlike what your usual first-aid box looks like, filled with bandages and antiseptics, this personalized kit focuses essentially on healing your mind and emotional imbalances. Think of it as a care package for your soul, always ready to support you whenever things begin to get overwhelming.  

 

What Exactly Is a Mental Health First-Aid Kit? 

 

It’s your go-to stash comprising of practices, habits, and tangible items that bring you instant peace and clarity of thought in tough times.  

It’s completely personal- tailor-made to fit your emotional needs. Your kit can be an ultimate game-changer, right from everyday stressors to every unexpected storm of life.  

 

Stocking Your Mental Health Toolkit 

1. Everyday Essentials: The ‘Band-Aids’ of Your Kit

 

These are the small, simple things that you can do to keep your everyday mental health in check: 

  • Breathing exercises: Breathe whenever in doubt. Deep inhalation and exhalation can work wonders for stress. 

  •  

  • Positive affirmations: Regularly remind yourself, “I’ve got this,” because you really do. 

  •  

  • Music therapy: Your favorite tunes can always lift your mood, almost instantly. 

  •  

  • Gratitude practice: Jot down three things you’re thankful for—it’s a proven mood booster.  

  •  

  • Mindful moments: Take a minute to savor your coffee or feel the morning breeze—it’s a very fruitful grounding exercise.

  •  

  • Creative outlets: You can create something that gives you joy. You could consider activities like doodling, cooking, or even gardening.  

 

2. The Heavy-Duty Tools: For When Life Hits Hard 

 

These are literally your ‘gauze and scissors’—the perfect strategies you turn to when things feel overwhelming than usual: 

  • Therapy or counselling: Sometimes, a professional perspective on things can help deal with your thoughts effectively.  

  •  

  • Support groups: Sharing personal experiences with others can help lighten the emotional load. 

  •  

  • Trusted friends or family: Try having a heartfelt chat with a loved one. It can truly feel very therapeutic.  

  •  

  • Social or spiritual communities: Being part of something bigger always provides a sense of belonging and hope. 

 

Building a Physical Kit 

 

Now, do you want to take it up a notch? Let’s create an actual physical box filled with items that bring you comfort and peace: 

  • A small candle or essential oil can work wonders for creating a calming aroma. 

Using fidget toys or a stress ball can help release nervousness/pent up energy. 

  • A notebook and pen to jot down feelings or affirmations. 

  • A coloring book and pencils are also fun examples of some therapeutic creativity. 

  • Give yourself sweet treats or mints for a quick pick-me-up. 

  • Pictures of loved ones or favorite places always spark joy. 

  • You can make positive notes—you can choose to write yourself a kind message or keep notes that you’ve received from others. 

 

Pro Tip: Personalize It 

Try to make your kit as unique as you are. It could be a playlist of your favorite songs, a piece of jewelry with a lot of sentimental value attached to it, or even a travel-size game for quick laughs. Remember! It includes whatever feels like you!  

 

Use It—Don’t Just Build It! 

A mental health first-aid kit only works if you actually make use of it. Whenever you feel stress creeping in or life taking an unexpected turn, instantly reach for your kit. And remember, sometimes the best kind of tool is asking for help—don’t hesitate to reach out to others when you feel in need of a little extra support. 

 

Why It Matters 

 

 

Just as we tend to stock up on supplies for physical emergencies, we must prepare for emotional challenges. Your Mental Health First-Aid Kit is your self-care arsenal—always ready to help you bounce back stronger, calmer, and more resilient than you ever were. 

So, what’s stopping you? Start building your kit today because, at the end of the day, peace of mind isn’t just a luxury—it’s a necessity.

title: Does Listening to Sad Songs Actually Make Us Feel Better
content:
Let’s picture this: It has been a rough day. You are feeling down and instead of reaching for something that lifts your mood instantly, you find yourself playing a sad song. Counterintuitive, right? Why would you choose to immerse yourself in sadness when you are already feeling low? Well, this is where science surprises you! According to a detailed study conducted by researchers Liila Taruffi and Stefan Koelsch from the Free University of Berlin, it was found out that listening to sad music has the power to boost your mood- and not worsen it. Welcome to the world of music therapy, where sad songs provide you the much-needed comfort, catharsis, and sometimes, even a bit of joy.  

So, what’s going on when you hit the “play” button?  

 

The Psychology Behind Sad Songs 

 

Taruffi and Koelsch’s study called participants to recall the emotions they usually experience when listening to sad music. Such feelings could be nostalgia, sadness, wonder, and even power. Interestingly, the topmost emotion reported by people was not sadness- it was nostalgia.  

This was followed by feelings of peacefulness and tenderness, painting a much more complex picture that goes beyond simply sorrow and despair. It turns out, the feelings triggered by sad songs often fall under the “sublime” category- emotions that may feel heavy but are always tinged with beauty.  

 

Sad Songs as Emotional Rewards 

The study also found out that people tend to turn to sad music to experience specific emotional rewards. Think of it this way: a sad song acts like your friend who gets you- someone who has been exactly where you are. When you listen to these songs, it lets you connect with your emotions without feeling vulnerable or judged. Instead of increasing your sadness, it gives you a release. It feels like letting out a big sigh.  

In fact, research also suggests that sad songs promote skills like empathy, imagination, and emotional regulation. So, when you feel low, listening to something that matches your mood helps you better process your feelings in a healthy way, giving you a small but meaningful boost. For many people, this effect is like a form of music therapy, offering you an accessible way of experiencing relief and emotional regulation outside the boundaries of formal counselling sessions.  

 

The Power of Nostalgia 

Why do sad songs bring up such deep feelings? Nostalgia is surely one reason. Think back to your college days- remember playing Hello by Adele on repeat after a tough breakup? Years later, that song might still trigger those memories, only now it may bring a smile on your face instead of tears. This is because music is very closely linked to our memories and emotions. As soon as you hear those familiar notes, you feel like travelling back in time.  

 

 

Sad Songs: Not Just a Psychological Thing—There’s Biology, Too 

As interesting as it may sound, sad music does not just play on our psychology; it impacts us biologically as well. When you listen to sad music, your brain begins to release a hormone called prolactin, which has a soothing effect on you. It feels like your brain is trying to comfort you through a kind of ‘emotional shield’. So, even though the song may be sad, the resulting effect is undoubtedly a calming effect.  

 

The Shared Connection in Sadness 

Another big reason for turning to sad music is to develop a sense of connection. When you are down, it is easy to feel like no one understands what you have been going through. A sad song instantly changes this. It’s a reminder to yourself that others feel the same thing that you have been feeling.  

 

Finding Beauty in Sadness 

Sad music also tends to have high aesthetic value. There’s something about a slow, soulful tune that captures the rawness of emotions in a beautiful, relatable way. Researchers Annemieke J.M. Van den Tol and Jane Edwards have found out that the more beautiful a song is, the easier it is to focus on it- and to feel the release that comes with confronting our emotions.  

 

Sad Music in Therapy and Counseling 

It’s no wonder, then, that mental health professionals are reading about sad music in music therapy and incorporating it as a supportive tool in counselling sessions. Sad music helps listeners connect with deeper emotions and process complex feelings, therapists tend to use it to help their patients explore difficult memories and deal with stress.

 

Next Time You’re Down, Try a Sad Song 

When life gets tough, sometimes we all need to have a good cry or a nostalgic throwback. It’s a healthy way to process emotions without brushing them aside. Son, the next time you are feeling down, do not be afraid to queue up for that sad song playlist. It might just be the boost your heart needs, even if it’s in the form of a tear or two.
