title: How does the NCAHP Act, 2021 affect psychologists? A Critical Analysis
content:
“The curious paradox is that when I accept myself just as I am, then I can change.”

– Carl Rogers

These wise words by the famous humanistic psychologist surely suggest that acceptance is the first step toward positive change. While many struggle with this paradox and seek help from therapists, the fate of these psychologists themself is something like a paradox only. 

In India, psychology is very under-identified and under-regulated. Due to this, there is a lack of quality control in education and training and literally, anyone starts calling themselves psychologists. The status didn’t change for many decades although there was a demand within the field itself to form a national council to regulate its affairs. 

Coming to the awareness that has been recently achieved due to the deadly virus outspread, one would expect government reforms to support psychologists, however, there is yet another disappointment for mental health professionals. 

Not many people in the psychology field know about this legislation and how it is going to affect their education and practice. And not everything in the new act is grossly erroneous. So, let us take a deep dive into the provisions and critically analyse keeping in view the lack of identity of the discipline. 

 

NCAHP Bill 2020: History of the legislation

On December 31, 2018, a Bill named Allied and Health Professions Bill, 2018 (“AHPB 2018”) was introduced in the Rajya Sabha by the Union Minister of Health and Family Welfare Mr. Jagat Prakash Nadda. Its objective was “regulation and maintenance of standards of education and services by allied and healthcare professionals and the maintenance of a Central Register of Allied and Healthcare Professionals.”

The next logical step was for the bill to be sent to the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Health and Family Welfare for examination and to produce its report. Due to the Lok Sabha elections, it took more than a year for the Standing Committee to finally present its report to the Parliament on January 31, 2020. Upon acting on the recommendations given by the Standing Committee, the Government revised the Bill and the Union Minister of Health & Family Welfare Dr. Harsh Vardhan introduced the new version as the National Commission for Allied & Healthcare Professions Bill, 2020 (“NCAHP Bill”) in the Rajya Sabha on September 15, 2020.

The Bill received the assent of the President on March 28, 2021 and became the National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions Act, 2021 (“NCAHP Act”) which came into force on May 25, 2021.

The NCAHP Act was formulated with the sole objective to provide “regulation and maintenance of standards of education and services by allied and healthcare professionals, assessment of institutions, maintenance of a Central Register and State Register and creation of a system to improve access, research and development and adoption of latest scientific advancement.”

The NCAHP Act is a landmark legislation intended to provide the much-needed regulation and standardisation. As the act has now come into force, the progression towards its implementation is underway. 

 

The NCAHP Act: Important provisions

 

  1. Definition of professionals:

The NCAHP Act defines two types of professionals; allied health professionals and healthcare professionals. 

Allied health professional: An allied health professional is ‘an associate, technician, or technologist trained to support the diagnosis and treatment of any illness, disease, injury, or impairment’.  Such a professional should have obtained a diploma or degree and the degree /diploma should be at least 2,000 hours (over a period of two to four years).

Healthcare professional: The healthcare professional ‘includes a scientist, therapist or other professionals who studies, advises, researches, supervises or provides preventive, curative, rehabilitative, therapeutic or promotional health services.’ They should have a qualification of degree with coursework of minimum of 3,600 hours spread over a period of three to six years.  

Allied and healthcare professions: The Act also specifies certain categories of allied and healthcare professions as recognised categories. These are found in the Schedule of the Act and lists around ten categories of professions:

1. medical laboratory and life sciences;

2. trauma, burn care and surgical/anesthesia related technology;

3. physiotherapy;

4. nutrition science;

5. ophthalmic sciences; occupational therapy; 

community care, behavioural health sciences and other professionals; 

medical radiology, imaging and therapeutic technology; 

medical technologists and physician associates; and 

health information management and health informatics professionals.  

In this article, we will focus on the ‘community care, behavioural health sciences and other professionals’ category of professionals. 

 

  1. National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions: The Act aims to set up the National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions consisting of a Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson and other specifically mentioned members consisting professionals from the healthcare industry. The Commission is formed to facilitate the framing of policies, regulating standards of education and practice, creating & maintaining an online Central Register of all registered professionals and provide for a uniform entrance/exit examination, just to name a few functions. 

 

  1. Professional Councils: For every recognised category of allied and healthcare professions, a Professional Council will be constituted consisting of a president and 4-24 members. This way each category of professional is represented adequately and the Commission can delegate some of its functions to such Professional Councils. 

 

  1. State Councils: According to the Act, within six months from the passage of the NCAHP Bill, state governments need to constitute State Allied and Healthcare Councils. The State Councils will: (i) enforce professional conduct and code of ethics to be observed by allied healthcare professionals, (ii) maintain respective State Registers, (iii) inspect allied and healthcare institutions, and (iv) ensure uniform entry and exit examinations.

 

  1. Establishment of Institutions: Prior permission from the State Council will be required to: (i) establish a new institution, or (ii) open new courses, increase the admission capacity, or admit a new batch of students to existing institutions.  If such permission is not sought, then any qualification granted to a student from such an institution will not be recognised under the Bill.

 

  1. Offences and Penalties: If someone uses the title or description of a profession mentioned in the NCAHP Act, 2021 without registration in the Central Register or a State Register, a fine of up to Rs 1 lakh may be imposed on the first conviction. On subsequent conviction, there is a provision of imprisonment up to 1 year and fine up to Rs 2 lakhs.

 

These provisions are important for regulating the professions and in fact in some ways long overdue. The Act also includes Movement Therapist (including Art, Dance and Movement Therapist or Recreational Therapist) under the Other Care Professionals category.

It is expected that teaching and research would receive major boost, with particular emphasis on learning practical skills. The lack of availability of supervision is a major issue in psychology right now, which is expected to be solved as after the implementation of this law, it would be mandatory for the institutions to create facilities for providing supervision.

Universities would require recognition as allied and healthcare institutions that mandates them to provide basic standards of education and necessary facilities in respect of staff, equipment, accommodation, training, and hospital.

 

Issues with the NCAHP Act concerning psychologists

While the act tries to provide for the missing regulation, there is silent negligence and ambiguity with respect to many issues. Let us uncover the issues with the Act with respect to the ‘community care, behavioural health sciences and other professionals’ category:

 

  1. The main concern is the name of the professional category. The Act uses ‘behavioural health’ instead of ‘mental health’ which is shocking because in India we have the Mental Healthcare Act 2017 and the National Mental Health Policy 2014. There is no explanation given to the readers and simply says that ‘behavioural health’ is the preferred term of usage. Why the sudden neglect and conflict of nomenclature with the existing legal terms. 

  2. Under the Mental Healthcare Act 2017, the clinical psychologists are ‘mental health professionals’, but under the NCAHP Act, other psychologists and counselors are ‘behavioural health sciences professionals.’ There is no apparent reason for the government to use different terms for the same discipline. This can create unwarranted conflict between professionals within the same field. 

  3. The definition of ‘behavioural health sciences’ in the Act mentions only the scientific study of emotions, behaviours and biology relating to a person’s well-being, completely ignoring the practice aspect of it. 

  4. Unlike the patient-centric provisions in the Mental Health Care Act, 2017 like informed consent, advance directive and restrictive alternative/environment, the NCAHP Act fails to attempt to protect the rights of the patients. 

  5. Clinical psychologists are excluded from the scope of this Act as they are governed by the Rehabilitation Council of India (“RCI”) Act, 1992. This seems alright but the strange part is that RCI comes under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment and the NCAHP is under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. It is absurd that one sub-field of psychology is regulated by one ministry and the other sub-field by another ministry. This depicts gross negligence and lack of knowledge on the part of the government. 

  6. It is blatantly observable that the name of the professional category is community care, behavioural health sciences and other professionals,’ not ‘behavioural health sciences professionals. As it was in the AHPB 2018. Additionally, this is the only category that has the term “other professions” as the professions mentioned under the same umbrella were vague and didn’t have any commonality. 

  7. Absence of a clear definition of “behavioural analyst,” “integrated behaviour health counselor,” “health educator,” “disease counselor,” “clinical social worker,” “psychiatric social worker,” “medical social worker,” etc., which are also included in the behavioural health sciences category.

  8. The Act mentions that the allied health professionals should have a degree or diploma with a coursework of minimum 2,000 hours spread over a period of two years to four years. This covers a bachelor’s degree too, however, the reality is that job opportunities after a bachelor’s is very rare and usually require a master’s to pursue a stable profession in psychology. 

  9. Another very shocking revelation has been the elimination of distance learning under the ambit of this Act.  While the idea behind is not malicious, what about those who have already pursued distance learning and acquired relevant experience, will they be discontinued? What about someone who pursued bachelor’s in the usual way and master’s through distance learning? All these questions remain unanswered. 

  10. Psychology is also very under-represented. The Professional Council for each profession sounds very reassuring but psychology comes under ‘Behavioural Health Sciences and Other Professionals’ Council’ and there wouldn’t always be a psychologist heading it. This kind of under-representation took place before as well. There was hardly any consultation with the psychologists during the drafting of the Mental Healthcare Act 2017. Even during the drafting of this Bill, there was virtually no consultation with the psychologists.

 

Change for the better or worse?

As far as psychology is concerned, there are serious concerns in the new Act. Starting from the inadequate definitions to inadequate representations and lack of clarity on the scope of professionals. The above-mentioned drawbacks are detrimental to the growth of the field that is so significant in this cultural climate. However, we have to keep in mind that the Act is mainly for the members of the medical community and the inclusion of psychologists seems incidental which is why not much thought has gone into structuring it better. 

 

The industry has been marginalised despite its history and significance. The government does make efforts to promote but the professionals are treated merely as a supporting staff to the bigger picture they have in mind. The real question is; how long will India ignore the importance of psychology? How long will we remain silent to ignorance? And exactly how long will we only give to get neglect in return?

title: How Effective is Self-Therapy? A realistic guide for beginners
content:
There are people who require mental health assistance but somehow feel restricted to take an actionable step. People usually enter the world of therapy in order to gain inner wholeness, overcome reservations and deal with their problems effectively. There are many ways in which one can accomplish that, the most traditional one is going to a therapist. But what if you could be your own therapist? Wondering how that works? There are a lot of reasons why people cater to self-therapy, the main reasons being geographical location, low-income status, or difficult access to therapeutic resources. Therefore, for a person who is unable to access a therapist for some reason or the other, is self-help or self-therapy the best option for them? Keep reading to find out!


Self-Therapy: Meaning 

The concept of self-therapy broadly refers to the idea of treating one’s own psychological or emotional issues by using different therapy techniques, all without the assistance of a professional. The term is essentially psychotherapies that we conduct on ourselves without the intervention of a professional therapist. Some of the ways in which self-therapies are practiced are achieved through books, online courses, step-by-step guides, and various other online free tools that are available. These self-help methods help you learn emotional skills and navigate relationships and life situations more effectively. In such cases, self-therapy can be highly effective and have a positive impact on your life.

Self-therapy cannot be considered a replacement for a professional therapist as there are many pieces of a professional session with a therapist that cannot be replicated via self-therapy. However, self-reflection remains a goal in self-therapy as well as therapy administered by a professional. Post your therapy session, it is up to you to self-reflect, and clear your thoughts to move towards the solution. Think of self-therapy as all of the above things except someone else helping you along the way. In self-therapy, you are your own therapist where you seek clarity and ask questions to yourself to understand yourself better.

There are many reasons why people prefer the self-therapy approach. Some may feel they don’t have enough time to spend or they can’t leave their homes or some may have a bad financial situation that is preventing them from having access to therapy. And now that we are talking about self-therapy if you were to take a step like that you must have a well-guided approach towards it.

How Effective is Self-Therapy?

Before going into the psychological findings that represent self-therapy vis-à-vis its effectiveness among people, it is crucial to understand that the likeliness of its effectiveness will depend on your unique symptoms and challenges as well as other sources you are using.

In 2017 there was a literature review that investigated how effective a self-guided internet cognitive behavioral therapy (iCBT) is for symptoms of depression. The review revealed that roughly 5 to 11 sessions of ICT were in fact effective enough to bring about a significant reduction in the symptoms of depression among the participants. The review was conducted over 13 studies that involved more than 3800 participants.

Another small study conducted in 2021 also explored the effectiveness of a self-guided virtual form of CBT and attempted to study people with panic disorder. The results revealed that 4 weeks of self-guided intervention actually helped people experience fewer or less intense symptoms.

Those who learn self-therapy also inculcate useful skills like CBT skills that one can apply to themselves to keep happy and healthy. You can easily learn many skills from CBT either with the help of your therapist or by finding an elaborate guide online. Skill building is one of the areas where self-help techniques really work. But then ideally the usage of all these self-therapy techniques runs parallel with your therapy sessions. The reason is that a professional will be there to give you a different perspective and guide you all through the way. A professional therapist can help you with a step-by-step guide to work on yourself as they process the information, we give them and build a trustworthy relationship with us. With the help of a therapist, you will have realizations and tools to help yourself that you otherwise wouldn’t have thought of.

Such findings definitely indicate that self-therapy is beneficial for certain mental health conditions. However, there isn’t much material to critique the technique of self-therapy. Therefore, it’s vital to understand that while self-therapy can help you be more honest and open with your emotions, it can also prove detrimental if it is misguided.

A self-guided therapy can be successfully performed only when you know what you are doing. Without proper knowledge of the same, you might end up messing up the process of your psychological intervention.


A Step-by-Step Guide to Self-Therapy: Things to remember

Usually, people who opt for self-therapy know what they’re signing up for either through their own research or their natural ability to look at things differently. However, they might be others who are struggling to understand self-therapy and how to apply the learnings in their lives. Having said that sometimes self-therapy exists to supplement your current session or make yourself feel better if you are having a bad day. There are other cases of course that need more personal attention in order to find mindfulness and wholeness from within. So if you’re going to guide yourself through the process of recovery you must make sure to follow the steps given:

Step 1- Understand the ambit of your problem. Is it a small problem or a big problem? Think of it as understanding your work or school assignment, is it something that can be done overnight or something which needs days of preparation? Once you understand what you’re dealing with it will be easier for you to comprehend if you can do this on your own or with some help.

Step 2- The second step is to study the problem from a deeper level. Like you would make subheads for your project, try splitting your problem into 2 parts, the feelings part and the action part. Once you understand the difference and the similarities you can start working towards taking actionable steps.

Step 3- The most vital step is to understand your emotions and feelings that are on the backdrop of your problem. Say your problem is a behavioral one, then you should try finding out the feelings that are causing such problematic behaviour.

These are all important aspects of self-therapy that one should consider before signing up for it. Although, sometimes it can be overwhelming and draining to do all of this on your own. So, if you feel stuck, don’t hesitate to seek professional help.

Signs you need to see a therapist instead of self-therapy

• Confused about your goals and whether or not your efforts are working.

• You feel overwhelmed by situations and emotions.

• You are unable to go on about your day-to-day and there’s a visible impact on your performance at work or school

• Use of substances as a coping mechanism.

• Struggle with relationships, sleep, or appetite.

• Gone through a very traumatic life event like death or divorce

• In case you have thoughts of self-harm or self-isolation.

If you can’t find the sunshine, then be the sunshine! Yes. Self-therapy can prove to be beneficial in our lives in many ways but it should be borne in mind that having a second person, a second perspective in the process makes it easier and more effective. Now with the advent of technology help can be received from the comfort of your home. Therefore, many barriers that initially stopped people from going to therapy are now being lifted. A therapist is a specialist in this field and only she will know the right way to guide you. The best way to go about it is the perfect blend of self-therapy and therapy from a professional.

title: How Effective Leadership Styles Can Improve Employee Morale
content:
If you had to choose between watching a funny dog video or spending five hours on a presentation your boss would tear apart, which would you choose? 

Think about it: some days you are required to coach and train, while on other days, you need to be visionary and motivational, setting an example for others to follow. 

 

Why Poor Management Drives Employees Away 

 

According to a Gallup study, 48% of employees were found to seek job change. Most people are calling it “the great resignation” and workforce gaps have become a global phenomenon. Although low pay is one of the contributing factors, another major reason is poor management and poor work environment.  

Poor environment at work clearly hints at a problem with management. No one likes to work with a toxic boss, and people also don't wish to put their best for someone whom they don't trust, like or respect.  

Leadership plays a pivotal role in shaping an organization’s culture and influencing employee morale. Good leaders set the tone by modeling behaviors and making use of the organization’s core values. Aspects like clear communication, accountability, and acknowledgement contribute significantly to fostering a positive culture and boosting employee morale. Inspirational leaders are those who build trust, empower their teams, and resolve conflicts to create a positive work environment.  

Therefore, effective leadership holds an organization together. Different types of leadership create a profound impact on the company’s culture and morale of its employees.  Therefore, it is extremely crucial for leaders to be mindful of this influence on their teams and on the organization in general.  

 

 

 

How Great Leaders Use a Mix of Styles to Succeed 

 

When it comes to how you lead your team, no one style can fit all. Every leader has a default leadership style, but to become an effective manager, you must learn other styles as well.  

One of the most important qualities of a good leader is their ability to adapt their leadership style according to the business environment, team members, and the ever-changing goals around them. Even a highly collaborative leader makes use of a combination of different leadership styles at different times- even in a single day. 

There is no set leadership style that every manager follows. Every leader is identified by their unique voice and individual approach to people and projects. It is important for you to acknowledge the different styles to know what might work best at different times, and what would help you achieve different purposes.  

 

Leadership Skills that Turn the Tide 

 

Manager-employee relationship is not a new concept. To take ancient wars as an excellent example in this case, just how good and efficient generals rallied their troops in the battlefield, similarly, CEOs and managers acquire the necessary skills to ensure their employees stay motivated and keep moving forward despite high stress and difficult times.  

Post-pandemic disruptions have left many working professionals and their leaders reeling. However, the companies that survived, and are still thriving, have one thing in common- employee stability.  

What we understand from here is that, even if high tensions impact employee motivation, the right leadership skills can instantly boost employee morale and turn the tables.  

What can high employee morale lead to? Better performance, lower absenteeism, and higher retention rates in any organization! 

 

 

Key Skills for Effective Leadership! 

 

Let us see how leadership and morale are interconnected, and what skills can help you make yourself into an effective leader!  

 

Trust building and transparency: Managers must ensure that their employees feel their opinions and concerns are heard and valued. Leaders can do so by fostering a culture of trust and transparency by being open and clear about their communication and the process of decision-making.  

 

Empowering and acknowledging employees: Employees must be given the freedom to make decisions and take ownership of their respective jobs. Recognizing their individual contributions helps boost their confidence and motivation.  

 

Provide opportunities of growth: In any organization, employees always seek progress in their careers and seek opportunities for learning and development. As a leader, you may offer training, mentorship, and opportunities of growth to help employees achieve their desired professional goals.  

 

Foster teamwork and effective collaboration: Teamwork and collaboration can effectively boost employee morale by creating a sense of belonging and togetherness among all. Leaders can ensure this by encouraging teamwork and setting up cross-functional teams and fostering a collaborative work environment.  

 

Lead by example: Any leader is an example for his team to follow. You should exhibit behaviors and values that you expect from your employees. How can you do that? By being approachable, respectful, and supportive.  

 

The Impact of Strong Leadership on Workplace Productivity and Morale 

 

In conclusion, leadership quality is extremely important for maintaining a positive and productive environment at work. Such an environment promotes employee morale and builds trust, empowers and recognizes employees, providing opportunities of growth, fosters teamwork and collaboration, and creates a culture of engagement, motivation, and high performance.

title: How Indian Athletes are Shaping Olympic History at Paris 2024
content:
From Dreams to Glory: How Indian Athletes are Shaping Olympic History at Paris 2024 

 

Indian athletes are etching their names in Olympics history. As the world watches and celebrates, India’s medal scoreboard shines with the excellence of our champions! Our athletes have turned dreams into glory, making the hearts of every Indian swell with pride!   

The 2024 Summer Olympics, officially called as the Games of the XXXIII Olympiad, now branded as Paris 2024, began from 24th July and will continue till 11th August 2024, in France. Paris is the host city, and the events have been spread across Metropolitan France.  

While Manu Bhaker opened the medal tally by winning a bronze for the nation in the 10m Air Pistol women’s event, and yet another in the 10m Air Pistol mixed team, Shooter Swapnil Kusale brought home another bronze in the 50m Rifle 3 Positions. What’s more, the Indian men’s hockey team won another bronze for the country, followed by Neeraj Chopra’s silver in the men’s javelin throw! Clearly, India has been shining brighter than ever, and our champions continue to make us proud! 

While all seem golden, people like Vinesh Phogat carried a heavy heart. What should not be forgotten here is how she became the first Indian to reach the Olympic final in women’s wrestling. She is not just a woman athlete but an ace Indian grappler who did suffer a major setback but also secured a silver for the nation.  

What does this tell us? True success lies in overcoming all personal setbacks like these. Vinesh Phogat’s story teaches us how resilience in the face of adversity leads us to extraordinary achievements and becoming the pride of our nation.  

 

 

The Hidden Struggles of Athletes' Mental Health 

 

Having said that, it also urges us to take a pause and reflect on the mental health of our athletes. Is a strong mindset a part of their personality? Well, it’s not the case as it seems!  

Exercise is well-known for impacting mental health in a positive way. However, it does not mean they are untouched by depression or anxiety. At the end of all that glory, we’re only humans seeking emotional balance.  

Athletes are usually admired for their physical prowess. However, what often goes out of notice is how despite their extraordinary skills, the demands of a good performance can weigh heavily on their mental health.  

Studies conducted in recent years, especially in medicine, sports and popular culture, mental health in athletes has earned more recognition. Factors like personality, intensive training, and fierce competition can trigger severe psychological issues among them.  

A 2019 study had highlighted how 35% of elite athletes suffer from mental health concerns. Athletes reported feelings of burnout, anxiety and depression as the top-rated issues.  

 

The Complex Causes of Mental Health Challenges in Athletes 

 

Mental health issues among athletes can result from a diverse range of causes: 

  • Stressful culture 

  • Nature of lifestyle 

  • Competitive nature of the environment  

  • Constant need for perfection 

  • Impact of social stereotypes and stigmas  

 

 

 

Inside the Mind of a Champion 

 

Several factors contribute to deteriorating mental health in athletes. Some of these have been discussed as under: 

Personality: 

Athletes tend to possess certain personality traits that help them succeed. However, these traits can also lead them to place tremendous pressure on themselves. The constant pressure to perform consistently and survive intensive training sessions can lead to increased levels of anxiety.  

 

Need for perfectionism: 

Sports teams often demand flawless game play. However, when someone overthinks their performance, it causes immense stress that can undermine their ability. When athletes underperform, they tend to question their self-worth, resulting in increasing fear of failure.

 

Bullying and hazing: 

Hazing refers to the practice of subjecting new players to rituals with an abusive nature. Such a practice can have severe short and long-term benefits on their mental health. What’s more, bullying, usually by coaches or peers, can cause feelings of exclusion, isolation, and low self-esteem. As a result, it develops depression, stress disorder or anxiety.  

 

Illnesses and injuries: 

When they suffer from an injury or illness, it can certainly prove to be stressful for anyone. Especially, injured athletes feel intensely pressurized to rehabilitate early and return to the field. Injuries can also lead players to get involved in substance misuse as they often try to self-medicate to heal as early as possible.  

 

Essential Tips for Athletes to Manage Stress & Boost Mental Health 

 

Talk to someone trustworthy: Reach out to a mental health professional, parent or a close friend. Perhaps someone in your team can relate to your experiences and emotions. 

Boost your social circle: Ensure that you keep positive, encouraging people nearby who significantly improve your perspective. Seek out more positive influences.  

Get a sound sleep: Your schedule may be controlled by training commitments. Thus, you must ensure that you go to bed early. That extra sleep will greatly benefit your physical and mental health.  

Maintain a good diet: There is a significant connection between nutrition and mental health. Nourishing your body requires you to maintain a nutritious and balanced diet.  

Pause to reflect: Understand the source of your stress and what triggers your internal battles. Negative thoughts are inevitable, however, acknowledging and accepting them is the first step towards keeping them in check.  

Invest in self-care: Do things that make you feel good about yourself. It could be an outdoor walk or solving a jigsaw puzzle. By focusing on self-care activities, your body releases “feel-good” hormones that help reduce stress.  

 

In the end, the true definition of success extends beyond medals and records. It is defined by the strength of character, the ability to overcome challenges, and the unconditional support we offer to those who inspire us. Here’s to celebrating not only our athletes’ commendable achievements but also their courage and determination in every phase of their journey. They have proved it: A strong mind makes champions shine!

title: How long does it take to become a counselor? - A realistic roadmap!
content:
Have you been thinking about helping other people? Does helping your friends and family solve a problem give you happiness? Are you thinking about becoming a counselor and entering the field of psychological aid? If the answer is yes to any of the above questions, then you are at the right place!

 

Counseling has grown out to become a thriving field with endless opportunities. For the longest time, consulting a counselor for emotional distress was taboo in India and many suffered the brunt of the backward mindset. Lately, people have been realising the importance of mental health and society has also started its course toward acceptance. This has opened up avenues of progress and opportunities for people who enjoy helping others.

 

If you are passionate about helping people, empathic toward others’ feelings, and wish to put your skills to good use, then becoming a counseling psychologist might be your career path. Although, once you decide to pursue your passion, you must have wondered how long it would take you to become a counselor? It is vital to assess and get educated about the field you are about to go after. Once you know the process and the amount of time you will have to invest in this lane, you are all set to make your mark in the field of counseling.

 

To understand how long it would take to become a counselor, let us delve into the step-wise account of the process of becoming a counselor in India.

 

What do counselors do?

 

A counselor is a person who specialises in helping people who are in need of support due to emotional difficulties. A counselor would be able to guide and nudge a person in the right direction concerning personal matters, career, lifestyle, and relationship difficulties. They are typically an intermediate between the individual and their problems. They work with individuals and groups to improve their mental health and well-being.

 

Some of the basic functions of a counselor include:

 

  • Assess and evaluate problems through various techniques like interviews and observation.

  • Conduct discussions with clients to understand the problem better.

  • Act as a facilitator to help the client achieve their goals.

  • Aid in developing alternative pathways to problem-solving.

  • Provide individual or group counseling for personal, educational, emotional, and social adjustment and improvement.

  • On the whole, take care of the client’s holistic mental well-being.

 

What are the different kinds of counselors?

 

Counselors are experts in guiding you with your issues that may arise from various spheres of your life like behavioural, personal, academic, etc. As a result, counselors can work in different domains, some of them are mentioned below:

 

Guidance and Career Counseling

When it comes to what you are about to do with your life, you need someone to show you the right way about your future. Here is where career counselors come into the picture. They help high school students, college students, and working professionals to find direction in their careers and resolve career-related issues.

 

Marriage and Family Counseling

There are always issues involving family members that are too uncomfortable or disturbing for people to manage. For instance, married couples often are in deep waters at the beginning and need counseling. Marriage or family counselors help individuals and groups understand each other and reduce conflicts and in return reduce mental stress.

 

Rehabilitation Counseling

These kinds of counselors deal with people with disabilities and help them enhance their personal, social and vocational life. Rehabilitation counselors work with both mental and physical disabilities including defects due to accidents, disease, etc.

 

Mental Health Counseling

Mental health counselors identify and treat emotional and mental disorders. They resort to therapeutic techniques to help people with depression, addiction, anxiety, trauma, grief, self-harm, etc. These counselors act as a resource when it comes to providing support which falls back emotionally and psychologically.

 

Substance Abuse Counseling

People who are addicted to drugs go through a tremendous amount of emotional distress along with a long-lasting effect on their families. Substance abuse counselors are specially trained to treat clients who suffer from addiction of any kind and employ techniques suitable for each case.

 

Educational Counseling

Educational counselors are focused on helping students achieve their true potential in terms of academics and co-curricular activities. Many students find it difficult to cope with studies and school and an educational counselor will be able to help students deal with social, behavioural, personal, and academic problems that arise at this crucial stage of their lives.

 

Steps to become a counselor in India: How long does it take?

 

Now that we know what a counselor does, let us look at how you can become one. There are essentially three basic steps and one optional step encompassing the process of becoming a counselor.

 

  1. Opt for Psychology as a subject in higher secondary

If you have already set your mind on psychology in school, then you can head start your career from higher secondary classes itself. Many schools offer psychology as part of their humanities stream and science stream. Ensuring psychology as part of your higher secondary studies will give you an edge over others in your bachelor’s. Some schools also have psychology as an option for all the streams, so a clever step would be to opt for psychology to get that basic insight on the subject. This step would last till the extent of your 11th and 12th grades.

  1. Pursue a bachelor’s degree (B.A. or B.Sc.) in Psychology (3 years)

Now the time comes to take your journey to the graduation level which is an important step to becoming a counselor. A typical bachelor’s degree would take 3 years in which you will learn about general psychology, counseling psychology, abnormal psychology, personality psychology, and statistics. You must also try to do internships and gain as much knowledge as possible.

While your degree will take care of your foundational knowledge, it is up to you to enhance your skills with training under people who can guide and help you out.

 

  1. Pursue a master’s degree in Psychology/Counseling/Applied Psychology (2 years)

Once you finish your bachelor’s you must pursue a master’s degree to gain practical experience in your field. And if counseling is your calling, opt for counseling psychology or applied psychology to learn about theories in counseling and the social issues that can arise out of it.

At this stage you complete your dissertation and internship as well, giving you a thorough picture of counseling psychology. This stage takes around 2 two years to conclude. Even if you did not pursue a bachelor’s in psychology, you can do your master’s, thanks to some colleges that do have that option.

 

  1. Pursue a PG Diploma in Counseling/Guidance (Optional 1 year)

Although you can start practicing as a counselor after your master’s from an RCI recognised institute, there is an option of doubling down your skills by doing a one-year diploma in guidance and counseling. Many institutes offer postgraduate diplomas to hone your counseling skills and gain certification in counseling. A diploma is a certificate course instead of a degree. Some people prefer to do a one-year diploma course rather than doing a two-year master’s degree.

 

Therefore, normally after your 12th grade, it will take you a minimum amount of five years to become a counselor depending on further specialisations and academic qualifications. Some also pursue Ph.D. along with work to accelerate their qualifications for better job opportunities.

 

Note: Registration with RCI is mandatory for using the title of 'Clinical Psychologist'. There is a distinction between Psychologists and Clinical Psychologists. However, by running a clinic, if one intends to practice clinical psychology including psychotherapy it is advisable to have RCI registration.

 

What are some of the tips to become a good counselor?

 

There is no hard and fast rule that you must possess all skills that a counselor needs before you begin your studies. The degrees and courses are precisely for that reason that they can equip you with the required skills. However, what efforts can be put in from your end to facilitate the learning? Let us take a quick look:

  • Be active in internships that offer practical experience.

  • Be open and accepting toward people.

  • Learn to listen and understand people.

  • Be calm and composed and avoid impulsive decisions.

  • Be relaxed and value your client as they would value your help.

These basic skills coupled with an openness to learning can land you at a very good place in counseling psychology.

 

Time to realise the importance of counseling!

 

Counseling is a very rewarding and illuminating profession. People who deal with all kinds of confusion and issues rely on counselors to help them toward self-realisation.

 

Now that we have seen how one can become a counselor in India and the steps involved, surely you can estimate how long it would take to become one. Access your foundational knowledge and take the big leap in psychology that you were waiting for!

title: How the NCAHP Act 2021 Supports Psychologists in India
content:
March 2021 marked a very significant date as India took the step towards strengthening the foundation of its allied healthcare professions with the fresh introduction of the National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions Act (NCAHP). The NCAHP Act was essentially designed with the primary motive of regulating and uplifting several allied health professions. This Act represents a huge milestone for emerging fields like Psychology, where standardized practices and professional recognition have been needed for much longer now. More than just a regulatory act, it promises to support and safeguard mental health services for both professionals and their clients.  

 

What the NCAHP Act Means for Psychologists

 

The NCAHP Act categorizes Psychologists under the broader classification of “Community Care and Behavioral Health Sciences Professionals”, giving it a prominent place within the larger framework of healthcare. This classification gives a formal acknowledgement to the field of Psychology as a vital component of the allied healthcare field and introduces a set of structured standards that impact psychologists in important ways.  

 

Standardized Training and Education 

Among the major benefits of the Act, one is the introduction of uniform training standards. It requires all institutions to meet specific educational criteria. By doing this, the Act ensures that students of Psychology and mental health practitioners receive consistent, high-quality training.  

This will be followed by regular audits of the programs to reinforce quality, assuring that students get to learn from approved and credible sources, and are prepared to face real-world challenges with enough experiential knowledge. On the other hand, clients benefit from this standardization as they can now place their trust on licensed professionals who meet rigorous requirements and uphold high professional standards.  

 

Professional Accountability and Recognition 

Furthermore, the NCAHP Act mandates the creation of a Central Register and State Registers for all licensed psychologists. This provides greater accountability to all professionals and simultaneously increases employment opportunities through the creation of a well-defined system for their respective professions.  

Such levels of accountability support public confidence in mental health services and offer a platform to all psychologists where their qualifications and ethical adherence are valued, acknowledged, and respected.  

 

Defined Scope of Practice and Roles 

The NCAHP Act also clearly outlines the roles and responsibilities that fall under each allied health profession, including psychology. For psychologists in India, this level of clarity is extremely crucial as it defines the scope within the broader realm of healthcare- diagnostic services to therapeutic support.  

With the practice of these guidelines, psychologists can better focus on their specialized skills without having to overlap their responsibilities with other mental health professionals, ensuring that they work within their unique areas of expertise.  

 

Psychologists’ Role in a Regulated Allied Healthcare System 

Psychology has evolved as an important aspect of mental health and emotional well-being in India. The Act’s regulations have put psychology at par with other healthcare professions like nursing and medicine, allowing all psychologists to collaborate effectively within multidisciplinary healthcare teams.  

With such structured support, psychologists can now integrate mental health care into broader healthcare settings in a more effective manner, contributing to a holistic and all-inclusive approach to emotional wellness in India.  

What’s more, this regulation also opens research and policy-making opportunities for aspiring psychologists, allowing them to bring their expertise to influence and impact healthcare decisions that ultimately affect the whole country. With such support, psychologists can advance their practices in line with the latest scientific developments and best industry practices, benefiting largely in terms of their profession and the clientele they serve.  

 

Key Provisions Benefiting Psychologists 

1. Central and State Registration – By registering with the Central or State Register, psychologists can become part of a community that is officially recognized. This recognition is very important as it provides them with a platform for ongoing professional development and growth. 

 

2. Curriculum Standardization – The NCAHP Act further establishes a clear set of standards for programs in psychology, ensuring that training is truly comprehensive, ethical, and up to date with modern day mental health challenges. This uniform curriculum prepares aspiring students for diverse scenarios in mental health care. 

 

3. Professional Ethics and Code of Conduct – Psychologists are now held to a unified code of ethics that strictly aligns them with other healthcare professionals. This unified code assures all clients of safe, respectful, and confidential treatment, thereby fostering a deeper culture of trust in mental health services. 

 

4. Eligibility Testing and Licensing – The Act also includes set provisions for a National Teachers Eligibility Test (NTET) and exit exams for all aspiring psychology professionals. These requirements strictly ensure that only qualified and capable individuals enter the profession, thereby protecting the highest quality and standards of mental healthcare and education in India. 

 

Why the NCAHP Act Matters for Mental Health in India 

The country’s need for mental health services has only grown, especially among younger generations. In today’s day and age, by setting such standards for mental health professionals, the NCAHP Act aims to address this evolving need by enhancing the accessibility and quality of mental healthcare. As this formalizes psychology as a carefully regulated healthcare profession, it simultaneously establishes it as a respected field, important enough to bridge the emerging gap between demand and the availability of qualified mental health practitioners.  

India is still a society where mental health is considered a social taboo. In this regard, the NCAHP Act plays a crucial role in validating the field of psychology as an important and crucial part of modern healthcare. It gives the sense of credibility to psychologists who need to practice with confidence and improves the way mental health is perceived, making it recognized as a legitimate and valuable service.  

 

Conclusion 

In conclusion, the NCAHP Act of 2021 marks a transformative and significant moment for psychologists working in India. It uplifts their credibility, provides a secure foundation for their professional growth, ensures standards and a structured framework. With top-notch education, a formalized support system at play, and strengthened ethical guidelines, psychologists in India are better positioned to make a meaningful impact in the mental health landscape.  

As India welcomes this new regulatory framework, psychologists can look forward to a promising future where mental health services are widely respected, accessible, and impactful for communities outlining the nation. Through this transformative act, mental health professionals and the common public can feel confident that the field of psychology is in capable, qualified hands!

title: How to become a counsellor
content:
You and I are part of a heavily competitive world where our responsibilities and goals have forced us to sideline our emotions and only focus on what can be achieved and accomplished. Almost everyone reading this would agree that the consequence of this ignorance has left us struggling in our life. We give in to parties and drown ourselves in alcohol or spend thousands just to take a quick trip as a means of escape and are still left longing for solitude. Our mental health keeps going downhill.  

This is the time when we wish to talk to someone who listens and understands; someone who can feel what we feel and give us solutions which may help. In the real world, we call them a counsellor. Their value and importance thus, is undeniable, especially in a country where worsening mental health is impacting the economy, relationships, and personal growth of individuals.  

 

A counsellor is a mental health professional who helps individuals deal with their personal challenges such as loss, addiction, trauma, and career transitions, by establishing trustworthy relationships and offering valuable support to their clients. In this regard, if you too are passionate about helping others and share a keen interest in the field of Psychology, this is the perfect time to pursue a career as a counsellor and embark on a fulfilling path for yourself.  

 

To begin with, you must possess some qualities that enable you to become a professional counsellor:  

  • Be willing to understand human needs and diverse perspectives, identify psychopathology, and assess concerns/problems. Your clients could come from diverse backgrounds such as students, young professionals, or even individuals dealing with emotional problems.  

  • Be able to integrate the core counselling skills like genuineness and empathy. 

  • Be able to apply and practice basic counselling skills including observation, active listening, reflecting feelings and thoughts, proper questioning, using silence when it is necessary, and much more in the process of counselling.  

  • Be able to make necessary therapeutic and developmental interventions when needed.  

  • Make an ethical code of conduct within the limits of counselling relationships.  

 

  •  

What is the scope of counselling in India? 

The scope of counselling is very broad. It focuses on various issues and developments that take place in an individual’s life, encompassing financial and health planning, family, societal, and emotional issues, among several other things. There is huge scope for counselling in major specializations like family counselling, career counselling, group counselling and client-centered counselling.  

The Times of India reports that the country urgently needs 15 lakhs+ counsellors to serve 315 million+ school children. These problematic figures highlight the need for immediate action. According to another survey conducted by India Times, schools in India need more counsellors as the percentage of students experiencing mental health issues continue to rise on an exceptional scale.  

 

Top career options for aspiring counsellors: 

 

Career prospects 

Average salary 

Career Counsellor 

Rs. 15,000-30,000 

Corporate Counsellor 

Rs. 20,000-80,000 

Credit Counsellor 

Rs. 17,000-30,000 

Genetic Counsellor  

Rs. 20,000-25,000 

Loan Counsellor 

Rs. 15,000-40,000 

Mental Health Counsellor 

Rs. 10,000-50,000 

Prison Counsellor 

Rs. 16,000-35,000 

Rehabilitation Counsellor 

Rs. 20,000-50,000 

 

Types of counsellors in India: 

The field of counselling is diverse and ever evolving with different types of counsellors. Based on their interests, qualifications, and experiences, counsellors usually specialize in more than one area of counselling. Let’s now explore the most popular types of counsellors in India: 

Clinical counsellors: 

They have a minimum of a master’s degree in psychology, counselling or education. They specialize in providing individual and group counselling services to couples, individuals and families.  

Educational counsellors: 

They help students and adults make decisions about their academic choices. They do so by offering guidance, advice, and support on academic goals, career planning, and educational performance.  

Mental health counsellors: 

They use diverse evidence-based techniques to help individuals manage their mental health issues like depression. addiction, anxiety and stress.  

Marriage and family counsellors: 

They provide couples, families and individuals with emotional support, practical advice and education on improving their relationships and refining their communication skills.  

Rehabilitation counsellors: 

They help people with physical, cognitive or psychological impairments adjust to life after suffering an injury or going through an illness. They make use of these techniques to improve the quality of life for their clients and their families.  

Career counsellors: 

They provide advice and assistance to people who seek employment or wish to explore career prospects that align with their interests. They help their clients understand their skills and points of interest and accordingly assess possible job options based on these qualities.  

 

 

Core counselling skills of a successful counsellor: 

Success is not guaranteed if you have pursued tons of degrees. To become a successful counsellor, you must acquire some relevant skills that help you understand the hidden factors and make you capable of delivering the best-personalized solution.  

Let’s shift our focus to the core skills when you’re considering a career in counselling: 

  • Active listening 

  • Rapport building skills 

  • Confidentiality 

  • Patience  

  • Empathy 

Becoming a successful counselor is more than just a career choice—it’s a commitment to making a profound difference in people’s lives. In a world where mental health issues are increasingly impacting individuals and society, the role of a counselor has never been more critical. Whether you're drawn to helping students navigate their futures, supporting individuals through personal struggles, or guiding families towards stronger relationships, there is a wide range of opportunities to make a meaningful impact. 

To excel as a counselor, it’s essential to cultivate key skills such as active listening, empathy, and patience, and to pursue the necessary education and licensing. The diverse specializations within counseling offer unique paths to cater to various needs and interests, from career counseling to mental health support. 

As India faces a growing demand for qualified counselors, especially within educational settings, now is an opportune time to step into this rewarding field. With dedication and the right qualifications, you can become a beacon of support, helping individuals overcome challenges and lead more fulfilling lives. Embrace this journey with passion and purpose, and you’ll be well on your way to making a lasting difference.

title: How to become an RCI Registered Psychologist in India?
content:
Practicing clinical psychology is a desired pursuit of many who aspire to work in the field of mental health. Clinical psychologists mainly work as highly trained professionals in the assessment, diagnosis, prevention, and treatment of mental disorders. Although they do not prescribe medicine, clinical psychologists use psychological techniques to inspire change in their clients. There are numerous ways to become a clinical psychologist, but a common factor among all methods is a license issued by the Rehabilitation Council of India (RCI) that regulates and monitors services given to people with mental health problems.

Earlier they typically worked in hospital settings wherein a clinical overview is required. The situation now though has changed, they are also being functionally used in schools, colleges, NGOs, universities, and private clients.

Every psychology student has at least once considered this stream of specialisation as it is the most popular and desirable one for those wishing to have their own practice, etc. In order to obtain an RCI license, certain eligibility criteria have to be met, and only then can you practice as a clinical psychologist. Even without having a psychology background, you can acquire certain degrees/ diplomas to be eligible for RCI approval.

Let us take a look at the need for an RCI license and the process for obtaining it.

Why is an RCI license important?

The RCI is the central regulatory body that monitors mental health services provided in the country. The body is responsible for research development, training, recognition, standardisation of curriculum, recognition of institutions, and registration of professionals. RCI maintains the Central Rehabilitation Register of all qualified professionals who work in the field of rehabilitation and special education.

Thus, in order to run your own clinic or practice as a clinical psychologist, an RCI license is mandatory. Licensed professionals have the authority to issue certificates for mental illness and are also authorised to speak on the subject of declaring a person mentally fit for trial in a court of law.

There are serious consequences for people practicing clinical psychology without an RCI license. The regulatory body can prescribe punitive actions against such people.

Eligibility for RCI Application

At the onset, you may be from any background as far as your bachelor's is concerned, but a master’s degree in psychology is one of the main prerequisites for RCI approval. A bachelor’s degree in psychology is desirable but even if you are not a psychology grad, you can pursue a master’s from universities and colleges that do provide such flexibility.

A checklist for RCI approval is as follows:

1. Master’s in Psychology: As discussed above, this criterion is a necessity, and a regular mode of education is usually preferred. Although, as long as you do your post-grad degree from an RCI-recognised university, you’re good to go.

2. Professional Diploma/M.Phil. In Clinical Psychology: The aim of doing a post-grad diploma is to acquaint you with theoretical inputs and practical clinical experience. Students who complete this stage are also eligible for specialised posts in various health care settings including schools, community centres, rehabilitation units, nursing homes, and so on. On the other hand, an M.Phil. will train you in diagnostic, therapeutic, rehabilitative, and administrative services in the clinical setup. Diplomas are usually concluded within a year and an M. Phil may be for a year or two depending on the institute. In both cases, the institution must be recognised by RCI and must have been undertaken in a regular mode of education. As far as education is concerned, with this criterion, you are eligible to apply for RCI.

3. Documents and Guidelines: The procedure for RCI license is given in detail on the website of the regulatory body as well. Going through it before starting the process will be a great first step. These guidelines contain a list of documents that are to be filed along with the form. Ensure the documents are ready digitally (scanned copies) to be uploaded/ submitted online. Be very careful while following the rules on documents and submissions.

Step – by step process of obtaining an RCI license

Once you go to the RCI Registration website, here are the steps in brief:

1. An application under the RCI Act, 1992 will have to be filled with a form fee of Rs. 1000/. Make sure to fill in the details cautiously and as per the info in your M. Phil. completion certificate.

2. Submit the documents asked by the portal (the website takes out lists and guidelines regarding the applications). Make sure they are scanned.

3. Take out the form given by RCI and get it filled out from your M.Phil. (or PG Diploma) institute that is of course recognised by RCI. This will serve as the Certificate of Authentication.

4. Once submitted, you shall get a Provisional Registration Certificate that shall be valid for a year.

5. Make sure to send all the documents offline as well to the postal address of RCI within 10 days of submitting the forms.

6. Once your license is ready, the official website portal will update the status of your application. You can keep a check on the site and once you get it, you are now an RCI registered psychologist.

Your career in psychology is on the rise!

All things aside, it is important to gain enough expertise in psychology to practice as a clinical psychologist which is why the RCI demands specific requirements. Recently, the RCI also released a list of RCI-approved Diploma courses in Special Education. The changes and efforts are afoot and if this is your calling, falling these steps will ensure a place for you in the clinical practice. The opportunities are also on the rise once you have RCI registration, making this a crucial step in your professional career. However, if you don’t wish to practice as a clinical psychologist, you don’t have to get an RCI registration. Thus, make sure to find your path of focus and work toward that.

title: How to choose internships in psychology in India?
content:
“Both optimists and pessimists contribute to society. The optimist invents the aeroplane, the pessimist the parachute.”

-       Sigmund Freud

 

This quote by none other than the father of psychoanalysis really makes you think about how every person on earth has something to offer, something to contribute. Likewise, now that you have made the decision to make a career out of the noble profession, psychology, you too have a lot to offer to the society.

 

As a psychology aspirant, you are constantly looking for opportunities to upskill yourself and equip yourself with the right qualities required to excel in the field. An internship in psychology is one such crucial part of gaining that practical knowledge you have been waiting for. The first-hand experience that you obtain provides you with a real-world perspective as opposed to the lectures and academics you are already going through.

 

Not all psychology students mandatorily require internships to graduate, at least at the undergraduate level. However, at the post-graduate level, you are required to pursue internships in your specific sub-fields to complete your degree. It is to be kept in mind that not all internships will be paid opportunities, they are by large voluntary. You might be doing some basic work but it definitely counts as a great learning exposure. Besides, you can learn a lot by just observing and internships can give you a sneak peek into the actual working of the world.

 

Ultimately, it is your choice whether you want to do an internship or not. But how do you make that choice? How to know which one is the right internship for you? And which experience will benefit your unique interests and skills? Keep reading to know how to choose the right internship in psychology in India.

 

Benefits of psychology internships

 

It has been established quite firmly that internships do provide you with practical skills, something you cannot possibly achieve from your classrooms. In fact, the theory part that you learn in college can be put to work in a professional setting through internships. 

 

Looking at this from a different perspective, internships can give you confidence and help you market yourself better during job interviews. Additionally, recruiters are also looking for people who have had some sort of exposure in the field of their liking. And of course, you learn plenty of skills during these internships that will shape your existing skills to do better in the field. It is true that each person possesses different skills and aptitudes and will develop their unique set of skills at the end of the internship tenure. It is advisable to communicate your goals and aspirations from an internship to your supervisor to get the best out of the opportunity. Let us look at some of the basic skills you will gain during an internship:

 

How to listen?

Probably one of the formative skills a psychologist requires is how to listen. Learning how to truly listen is no cakewalk and takes immense practice and patience. 

 

How to communicate?

Along with listening comes communication which is equally an important aspect of becoming a successful psychologist. Not only will you carefully listen to your clients, but you will have to learn how to effectively communicate with them as well. 

 

How to be empathetic?

It is vital that you learn how to deal with your feelings and emotions while listening to your client. Being empathetic has nothing to do with feeling bad for your client but being able to feel what they must have felt, or being in their shoes. This will refine your response and accelerate growth within the clients as well. 

 

How to deal with diversity?

It is very common in psychology to meet new people every day and deal with them, so, as an upcoming psychologist, you need to enable yourself to work with all kinds of people. An internship will let us experience it!

 

How to be a problem solver?

As said earlier, interns have a shot at observing professionals and how they handle their challenging jobs. A great deal can be learned about dealing with situations of difficulty and using analytical skills to solve problems.

 

These are just some qualities you will acquire from an internship besides a few other skills with respect to your specialties. 

 

Looking for psychology internships? Where to look?

 

Internships are for all and everyone in the field of psychology. Whether you are someone pursuing a full-time degree from a college or someone who is planning to enter the field, there are numerous opportunities awaiting you. By taking the right steps you can land yourself the perfect internship!

 

Assess yourself

The first step is to comprehend your interests and goals to be achieved before looking for internships. It would be beneficial to plan your career path beforehand or maybe just a rough roadmap. If you are a full-time college student, plan your subject choices and lay out a clear path for yourself. In case you are pursuing distance learning or entering psychology from a different field, you will be able to assess yourself better as your passion for the subject got you here. Educate yourself about various fields in psychology and the ways you can achieve them to select the path for you.

 

Traditional way 

The conventional way to procure internships is through your college's on-campus resources. Students who are pursuing psychology through traditional colleges have the advantage of using their institution's network to obtain appropriate opportunities. Approach your placement cell to get advice and select from the range of offers they can provide for you. However, you also have the option of accessing internships that are available online.

 

Distance learners and newbies 

Distance learners and people entering the field in unconventional ways need to focus on adopting a more direct approach concerning internships. During your search, you must look at opportunities in NGOs and social institutions that don’t necessarily mandate a psychology background. Psychiatrist institutions and rehab centers are also popular internship destinations. Although these opportunities can be availed by other seekers too, however, if you are a non-traditional aspirant, keep an openness to explore options available to you. Organisations that are into social work, basically not profit-oriented will work with less funding and the community at large. They are likely to help but may have limited opportunities to work with professionals as guides or mentors until further experience.

 

Online Internships

With technology and mental health reaching heights, you will find a plethora of breakthroughs on the internet. If you want to engage in an internship independently, a number of ads are posted by recruiters from time to time on sites like Naukri, Indeed, Internshala and LinkedIn. These popular recruitment sites have opportunities that can further your career. As psychology gains importance, the offers are also on a raise on such platforms. Many mental health organisations also provide online internships. Which an accessed on social media platforms like Instagram and Facebook. After COVID-19, the online market has skyrocketed with jobs that can be undertaken remotely. Many start-ups and companies have emerged that primarily focus on mental health, therefore extending your horizon of opportunities.

 

A few things to remember while choosing an internship

 

Build our network

It is important to connect with like-minded people and exchange thoughts and ideas. Networking within your workplace is very crucial to growth and development. Don’t be afraid to talk to your peers and widen your scope of networking. You’d be surprised at what they know about their community and work. You can get a good hold on the field. Social media sites are also recommended to reach potential internship locations. 

 

Seek guidance

You must talk to your professors for internships as they would have good contacts in the industry. Use the network available to you to procure work that you might not otherwise know about. Many schools and companies also offer career services to their distance learning students. Take advantage of these services, especially if your college has an internship department. 

 

Identify the work

It would not be wise to completely rely on online postings. Look for organisations and meet them in person to know the workplace better. If some don’t respond, don’t be disheartened and keep trying to seek internships. As they say, consistency is key! You will find the place that is right for you.

 

Contact professionals

 If you know professionals working at mental health institutions, use your connection as they are in direct touch with what you are seeking. You can also ask the professionals who work at these organizations for suggestions of other opportunities.

title: How to effectively handle work-related stress?
content:
You would be amazed to know that India reports a staggering growth of 70% of workers struggling with work-related stress at least once in every week! As surprising as it sounds, this statistic surpasses the Asia-Pacific average of 60%. In this blog, you will learn about the complexities of work-related stress, and learn about the most effective strategies that can help you develop a healthier, and more supportive work environment!

 

What is work-stress?

 

How do you define work-stress? The term ‘work-stress’ is used to refer to the physical, emotional, and psychological strain that an individual experiences in response to any work-related demand. This could be felt in the form of inevitable pressure and expectations.

 


 

Work-stress in organizational behavior:

 

Work-stress results from an imbalance between the demands of your job and your ability to cope with that demand. This imbalance creates an overwhelming feeling, a sense of frustration, and heightened exhaustion. Work-stress can manifest itself either through physical symptoms like fatigue or headache, emotional symptoms like anxiety or irritation, or behavioral symptoms like absenteeism or decreasing productivity. Therefore, a chronic exposure to work-stress can severely affect your physical & mental health, thereby impacting your overall performance and wellbeing.

 

In the context of organizational behavior, work stress can be defined as the phenomenon of stress which is experienced by people within a typical workplace setting.

 

This kind of stress can be influenced by several factors: 

1. Workload

2. Role ambiguity

3. Interpersonal conflicts

4. Lack of control

5. Organizational culture

 

Work-stress in organizational behavior affects an employee’s attitude, behavior, and work performance. This field is studied from multiple perspectives, which include individual, group, and organizational levels to understand its causes, consequences and all other potential interventions.

 

How does studying organizational behavior help?

 

Organizational behavior attempts to identify effective strategies that can help promote these 3 things:

1. Employee wellbeing

2. Improving organizational effectiveness

3. Creating a healthier work environment

 


 

Can work-stress affect your mental and physical health? Here’s what you should know!

 

A stressful work environment can create several problems like irregular sleep, temperament issues, frequent headaches, stomach ache, and difficulty in concentrating. If not paid heed to, this stress can eventually develop into a chronic problem, creating insomnia, high blood pressure, or even a weakened immune system and anxiety! 

 

Remember!

 

If you have already been suffering from health conditions like heart disease, obesity, or depression, work stress can add to your misery. Therefore, in an attempt to cope up with this, instead of turning to unhealthy habits like overeating, junk food, smoking, or use of alcohol and drugs, you must seek out healthy ways that will help you in the long run. 

 

Looking for some tips? Here you go!

 

Work-stress management: 

 

1. Keep a check on your stressors: Did you feel an intense pain in your forehead or raise your voice or did you go to the snack counter immediately after having a stressful event? Here’s where journaling can help. Recording your thoughts, feelings, and details about the atmosphere, people and situations can help you identify specific situations which created the most stress and how you respond to them. 

 

2. Start off your day on a good note: Having a stressful day depends on how you begin your day. Hence you should avoid having a stressful morning as much as possible. If you begin your day with effective planning, nutrition and a positive attitude, you will be able to tackle a good amount of stress at your workplace or let it roll off easily. 

 

3. Be clear about what you need: When you don’t know exactly what you are required for and your role keeps changing with little or no notice you might feel extremely pressured or stressed. In such a case, make sure to talk directly to your supervisor. It is always a good idea to go over your expectations and discuss ways for you to meet them accurately without it being stressful for you or your employer.

 

4. Develop a healthy response: Any kind of physical activity acts as a very good stressbuster and helps you release the work-related pressure that you have been carrying. Some examples could be exercise, yoga, playing games with your family, or even reading a book. Additionally, good quality sleep is also essential for effective stress management. Build healthy habits, limit your caffeine intake, and screen time, and engage in leisure activities that allow you a window to breathe.

 

5. Establish boundaries: Establishing boundaries at work is important but you must also have some work-life boundaries for yourself. This allows you to set a time for yourself to check your mail and keep your phone aside when  you are on a break. These habits will help you reduce potential work-life conflict and the stress that accrues out of it.

 

6. Forget about multitasking: multitasking allows you to maximize what you can do with your time. However, its major downfall is, with so much going on at the same time, you find it extremely difficult to split your focus and oftentimes, it doesn’t work well for most people.

 

These are some of the most effective ways you can handle work-related stress without feeling overwhelmed or burdened. Seek help from the friends and family members you trust the most, whenever you are unable to manage stress. Ask your employer for stress management resources (if any) and go through other resources like online information, counseling, and consulting mental health professionals. If you still feel a burn out, you must see a psychologist and seek help to tackle your stress effectively.
